item.content:encoded:
The University of Southern Queensland (UniSQ) is inviting applications for its International Stipend and Fee Research Scholarship (DPHD) for international students who will commence or continue a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) in 2027.

The scholarship provides successful applicants with a tax-free stipend of AUD $39,000 per year as well as coverage of tuition fees for up to three years of full-time equivalent PhD study.

Applications are welcomed across all research areas, provided the proposed research aligns with one of UniSQ’s flagship research areas. The scholarship is designed to support high-achieving international researchers who demonstrate strong academic performance, research capability, and a well-developed research proposal.

About the UniSQ International PhD Scholarship

The International Stipend and Fee Research Scholarship is a competitive research scholarship for international students pursuing doctoral research at UniSQ.

The scholarship combines the stipend and tuition-fee components into one application. Applicants do not need to apply separately for the stipend and tuition-fee scholarship.

Successful scholars will have the opportunity to undertake doctoral research within UniSQ’s research environment while receiving financial support for their studies.

Applicants are encouraged to explore UniSQ’s available research thesis topics and identify potential supervisors whose expertise aligns with their proposed research.

Scholarship Benefits

The UniSQ scholarship provides substantial financial support throughout the doctoral programme.

AUD $39,000 Annual Stipend

Successful applicants will receive a stipend of:

AUD $39,000 per annum

This financial support is intended to assist scholars with living and study-related expenses while undertaking their PhD.

Full Tuition Fee Support

UniSQ will pay tuition fees for a maximum period of:

Three years of full-time equivalent study

The scholarship covers the applicable tuition fees during the supported period.

However, any period of study already undertaken towards the PhD will be deducted from the scholarship period.

Research Areas

Applications are welcomed across different areas of research, but proposed projects must align with UniSQ’s flagship research areas.

Applicants should discuss the flagship area that most closely matches their proposed research with their potential supervisor before submitting their application.

This alignment is important because applicants are assessed partly on the relationship between their proposed research and UniSQ’s research priorities.

Prospective applicants can also explore UniSQ’s current research thesis topics and connect with UniSQ experts to identify appropriate research opportunities and potential supervisory arrangements.

Industry Stream

The scholarship also provides an optional Industry Stream.

The Industry Stream is designed to create stronger connections between doctoral research and industry by requiring successful participants to complete a:

60-day industry internship

Applicants interested in this stream are responsible for identifying an appropriate industry partner, either independently or with support from their prospective supervisor.

The industry partner must complete a Letter of Support as part of the application.

If the scholarship is awarded under the Industry Stream, all required contractual agreements must be completed before the student begins the programme.

Continuing Student Requirements for the Industry Stream

Continuing students applying for the Industry Stream must meet additional timing requirements.

They must be:

  • Within 18 months of commencing full-time study, or
  • Within 36 months of commencing part-time study.

Applicants are advised to consult UniSQ’s Senior Coordinator for Commercialisation and Partnerships before applying to ensure that the proposed internship meets the university’s requirements.

Dedicated Opportunities for Women in STEMM and Students With Disabilities

In addition to the Industry Stream, the scholarship offering includes dedicated scholarships for:

  • Women in STEMM
  • Students with disabilities

This provides additional opportunities for applicants from groups specifically supported through UniSQ’s research scholarship offerings.

Applicants should review the relevant scholarship requirements when preparing their application.

Eligibility Requirements

To be considered for the UniSQ International Stipend and Fee Research Scholarship, applicants must meet the university’s eligibility requirements.

Applicants must:

Hold the Required Academic Qualification

Applicants must have completed a Bachelor Degree with First Class Honours, or an equivalent qualification.

Applicants should provide evidence of their academic qualifications and transcripts as part of the application.

Be Eligible for Full-Time PhD Study

Applicants must be eligible to enrol full-time and on-campus in the Doctor of Philosophy programme at UniSQ.

The scholarship is therefore intended for students who satisfy the university’s requirements for admission to its PhD programme.

Be an International Student

Applicants must be international students.

They must not be:

  • Australian citizens
  • New Zealand citizens
  • Australian permanent residents

Commence or Continue Study in 2027

Applicants must either:

  • Commence their PhD studies in 2027, or
  • Continue their existing PhD studies in 2027.

Academic and Research Selection Criteria

Eligibility does not automatically guarantee a scholarship.

Applications are assessed using several selection criteria designed to identify applicants with strong academic and research potential.

Academic Achievement

The university considers applicants’ academic records, including:

  • Honours classification or equivalent
  • Performance in postgraduate study
  • Academic prizes
  • Academic awards
  • Overall academic achievement

Applicants with a strong academic history are therefore likely to be more competitive.

Research Capability

Applicants are also assessed on evidence of their ability to conduct high-quality research.

Relevant evidence may include:

  • Research publications in high-quality journals
  • Conference presentations
  • Research internship experience
  • Creative works, where applicable
  • Other evidence demonstrating research capability

Applicants should clearly demonstrate their previous research experience and achievements.

Research Project and Environment

The proposed PhD project is another important part of the assessment.

The university may consider:

  • Alignment with UniSQ research priorities
  • Relevance to the Australian research context
  • External support for the proposed research
  • Potential impact of the research
  • Resources required to successfully complete the research

Applicants should therefore ensure that their research proposal is clear, realistic, relevant, and well aligned with UniSQ’s research strengths.

Supervisory Team

The proposed supervisory team is also considered.

Applicants are encouraged to work closely with prospective supervisors and demonstrate:

  • The supervisors’ publication records
  • Complementary research expertise
  • Supervisor capacity
  • Available resources to support the proposed research

Finding an appropriate supervisor before applying can therefore be an important part of preparing a competitive application.

PhD Admission Is a Separate Process

An important requirement is that applying for the scholarship and applying for admission to the PhD programme are separate processes.

Applicants must begin the application process for admission into the Doctor of Philosophy programme in order to be eligible for the scholarship.

Prospective students should therefore allow sufficient time to complete both processes.

Required Application Documents

Applicants should prepare digital copies of the required supporting documents before beginning the scholarship application.

These include:

  • Statement of Claim completed by the student and supervisor
  • Curriculum vitae, including research publications and/or presentations
  • Preliminary Research Thesis Topic Proposal
  • Documentation confirming citizenship
  • Testamurs and academic transcripts for all undergraduate and postgraduate qualifications

Applicants applying through the Industry Stream must also provide:

  • Letter of Support completed by the industry partner

All documents should be prepared carefully and submitted according to UniSQ’s application requirements.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should follow the university’s application process.

Step 1: Identify Your Research Area

Review UniSQ’s flagship research areas and identify the area that most closely aligns with your proposed PhD research.

Step 2: Find a Potential Supervisor

Applicants should connect with a potential supervisor whose research expertise matches their proposed project.

Discussing the proposed research with the supervisor can help applicants refine their research direction and identify the appropriate UniSQ flagship area.

Step 3: Begin the PhD Admission Process

Applicants must start the separate application process for admission to the Doctor of Philosophy programme.

Step 4: Prepare the Scholarship Documents

Prepare the required academic records, CV, research proposal, Statement of Claim, citizenship documentation, and other supporting materials.

Step 5: Submit the Scholarship Application

The scholarship application must be submitted through the UniSQ Scholarship Application Management System before the closing date.

Application Portal: https://scholarships-apply.usq.edu.au/

Applicants who need assistance can consult the university’s Scholarship Online Application Manual.

Application Deadline

The closing date for the scholarship is:

27 September 2026

Applicants should submit their applications before the deadline and allow enough time to obtain supporting documents and complete the separate PhD admission process.

Who Should Apply?

This opportunity is particularly suitable for international students who:

  • Have completed a Bachelor’s degree with First Class Honours or equivalent
  • Have strong academic achievements
  • Have research experience or demonstrated research capability
  • Have a clear and original PhD research idea
  • Want to pursue doctoral research in Australia
  • Can align their proposed research with a UniSQ flagship area
  • Are able to enrol full-time and on-campus
  • Plan to commence or continue their PhD studies in 2027

Researchers with publications, conference presentations, research internships, or other evidence of research capability may be particularly competitive.

Why Consider the UniSQ Scholarship?

Pursuing a PhD internationally can involve significant tuition and living costs. This scholarship can substantially reduce the financial burden by combining an annual stipend with tuition-fee support.

The AUD $39,000 annual stipend provides financial assistance throughout the supported scholarship period, while UniSQ covers tuition fees for up to three years of full-time equivalent study.

The opportunity also provides access to a research environment where doctoral candidates can work with experienced supervisors and engage with research projects aligned with UniSQ’s flagship areas.

The optional Industry Stream adds another dimension by providing an opportunity for eligible scholarship recipients to undertake a 60-day industry internship.

Important Considerations Before Applying

Applicants should not wait until the final days before the deadline to begin their applications.

Finding a suitable supervisor, developing a research proposal, obtaining academic documents, and completing the separate PhD admission process can require considerable preparation.

Applicants should also ensure that their proposed research is genuinely aligned with UniSQ’s research priorities and that they can clearly explain the expected contribution and impact of their project.

For the Industry Stream, applicants should begin discussions with a potential industry partner early enough to obtain the required Letter of Support and complete any necessary agreements.

Conclusion

The UniSQ International Stipend and Fee Research Scholarship 2027 is a significant opportunity for high-achieving international students seeking to undertake PhD research in Australia.

Successful applicants can receive AUD $39,000 per year and tuition-fee coverage for up to three years of full-time equivalent study. The scholarship welcomes research proposals across multiple areas, provided they align with UniSQ’s flagship research priorities.

In addition to the standard scholarship, applicants can explore the optional Industry Stream, which includes a mandatory 60-day industry internship, as well as dedicated opportunities for women in STEMM and students with disabilities.

With a deadline of 27 September 2026, prospective applicants should begin preparing their research proposal, identifying a potential supervisor, gathering supporting documents, and starting the separate PhD admission process well in advance.

Discover more opportunities on the OFY Webpage.

item.content:encoded:
The Digital Education Council (DEC) Postgraduate Research Fellowship 2026 is a new research-focused opportunity designed for postgraduate researchers who are interested in artificial intelligence, digital education, higher education, and emerging issues shaping the future of learning. The fellowship aims to strengthen the Digital Education Council’s global research agenda by bringing talented researchers into its international research activities. Selected fellows will have the opportunity to contribute to the design and delivery of DEC’s global Working Groups while supporting the development of research publications focused on artificial intelligence and other rapidly developing issues in higher education.

With artificial intelligence transforming teaching, learning, assessment, academic research, university administration, and the wider higher education ecosystem, this fellowship provides an opportunity for postgraduate researchers to engage directly with research questions that are increasingly important to universities and education policymakers around the world.

Application Deadline: Monday, 14 September 2026

About the Digital Education Council Postgraduate Research Fellowship 2026

The Digital Education Council Postgraduate Research Fellowship is intended to support and expand DEC’s global research activities.

The programme connects postgraduate-level researchers with an international research agenda focused on digital transformation in education. Fellows will work alongside DEC’s broader research activities and contribute to initiatives examining how emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence, are influencing higher education.

Rather than being limited to traditional academic research conducted independently, the fellowship is designed around practical engagement with DEC’s global Working Groups and research publications.

This means selected researchers can potentially gain experience in areas such as:

  • Higher education research
  • Artificial intelligence and education
  • Digital transformation
  • Emerging technologies
  • Research publication development
  • International research collaboration
  • Higher education policy and practice
  • Global education trends
  • Research-driven Working Groups

What Will Selected Fellows Do?

Researchers selected for the 2026 Postgraduate Research Fellowship will support two important areas of the Digital Education Council’s work.

1. Support DEC Global Working Groups

One of the key responsibilities of fellows will be to support the design and delivery of DEC’s global Working Groups.

Working Groups provide a setting for researchers and other stakeholders to examine important issues affecting higher education and digital education.

By contributing to these activities, fellows may gain exposure to collaborative research processes and international discussions surrounding emerging technologies and higher education.

This can be particularly valuable for postgraduate researchers who want experience beyond their individual academic research projects.

2. Contribute to Research Publications

Fellows will also contribute to the development of research publications on artificial intelligence and other burgeoning issues in higher education.

Artificial intelligence is developing rapidly, creating new research questions for universities, researchers, educators, students, and policymakers.

Potential areas of research interest may include questions surrounding the impact of AI on higher education, the adoption of emerging technologies, digital transformation, and the changing role of universities in an increasingly technology-driven environment.

Through participation in publication development, fellows can gain experience contributing to research intended for a broader international audience.

Why This Fellowship Matters

The higher education sector is undergoing significant technological change. Artificial intelligence has introduced new possibilities for teaching, learning, research, assessment, student support, and institutional decision-making.

At the same time, universities are facing important questions about how these technologies should be implemented responsibly and effectively.

The Digital Education Council’s fellowship responds to this changing environment by bringing postgraduate researchers into research activities focused on AI and other emerging issues.

For researchers interested in the future of education, this can provide an opportunity to connect their academic interests with current global discussions.

Potential Benefits of the Fellowship

Although the provided fellowship announcement does not specify a comprehensive list of financial or additional benefits, participation in the programme can offer researchers valuable professional and academic exposure through the activities described by DEC.

Potential areas of value include:

Research Experience

Fellows will have an opportunity to contribute to research activities connected to artificial intelligence and emerging higher education issues.

International Research Exposure

Because the programme supports DEC’s global research agenda and Working Groups, fellows can engage with research activities that have an international perspective.

Publication Experience

Contributing to research publications can help postgraduate researchers develop practical experience in producing research for audiences beyond their immediate academic institution.

Collaboration

The fellowship provides an opportunity to participate in collaborative research activities rather than focusing exclusively on individual academic work.

Understanding of Emerging Issues

Researchers can deepen their understanding of rapidly developing topics affecting higher education, particularly artificial intelligence and digital transformation.

Professional Development

Working on international research initiatives can strengthen a researcher’s experience and provide valuable exposure to contemporary issues in higher education research.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The fellowship is particularly relevant to postgraduate researchers whose academic or research interests connect with areas such as:

  • Artificial intelligence
  • Higher education
  • Educational technology
  • Digital education
  • Digital transformation
  • Emerging technologies
  • Education policy
  • Technology and learning
  • Higher education innovation
  • Research into the future of universities

Researchers whose work intersects with AI and other emerging issues in higher education may find this opportunity especially relevant.

Key Areas of Interest

Applicants interested in the fellowship may want to consider how their research connects to the broader questions currently affecting higher education.

Some potentially relevant themes include:

  1. Artificial Intelligence in Higher Education
    Research examining how AI is being adopted and used by universities, educators, researchers, and students.
  2. The Future of Digital Education
    Research exploring how digital technologies are changing educational systems and learning environments.
  3. Emerging Technologies
    Studies examining technologies that could influence the future direction of higher education.
  4. Higher Education Transformation
    Research focused on how universities are adapting to technological, social, and institutional changes.
  5. Education Policy and Technology
    Research exploring the policy implications of new technologies in higher education.
  6. Responsible Technology Adoption
    Research examining how emerging technologies can be implemented effectively and responsibly within higher education.

Important Information About the 2026 Fellowship

Detail Information
Opportunity Digital Education Council Postgraduate Research Fellowship
Year 2026
Organiser Digital Education Council
Focus Research, AI, digital education and emerging issues in higher education
Main activities Supporting global Working Groups and contributing to research publications
Target group Postgraduate researchers
Application deadline Monday, 14 September 2026

Application Deadline

The application deadline for the Digital Education Council Postgraduate Research Fellowship 2026 is:

Monday, 14 September 2026

Prospective applicants should make sure they allow enough time to review the official application requirements, prepare their materials, and submit their application before the deadline.

Waiting until the final day can create unnecessary risks, particularly if additional information or supporting materials are required during the application process.

Apply HERE

How to Prepare for the Fellowship Application

Researchers considering this opportunity should take time to clearly connect their academic background and research interests with the fellowship’s focus.

A strong preparation strategy may include the following:

Step 1: Review Your Research Interests

Identify the main research questions, themes, or topics you are currently working on.

Consider whether your research connects with AI, higher education, digital education, emerging technologies, or another area relevant to DEC’s global research agenda.

Step 2: Understand the Fellowship’s Research Focus

Read the official fellowship information carefully and understand what DEC expects from researchers participating in the programme.

Pay particular attention to its emphasis on global Working Groups and research publications.

Step 3: Highlight Relevant Research Experience

When preparing your application, emphasize research experience that demonstrates your ability to contribute meaningfully to collaborative research activities.

This could include academic research, publications, research projects, conference participation, policy research, or other relevant work where applicable.

Step 4: Demonstrate Your Interest in Emerging Issues

The fellowship is closely connected to AI and other burgeoning issues in higher education.

Applicants should therefore be able to demonstrate genuine interest in how emerging technologies are affecting the higher education sector.

Step 5: Prepare Before the Deadline

Do not wait until the deadline to begin preparing your application.

Aim to complete your application early enough to review it carefully and correct any missing or inaccurate information before submission.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the Digital Education Council Postgraduate Research Fellowship 2026?

It is a new research fellowship programme from the Digital Education Council designed to support and expand its global research agenda by involving postgraduate researchers in its research activities.

What will fellows work on?

Selected researchers will support the design and delivery of DEC’s global Working Groups and contribute to research publications concerning AI and other emerging issues in higher education.

Is the fellowship focused on artificial intelligence?

Yes. Artificial intelligence is one of the central research areas identified in the fellowship description, alongside other rapidly developing issues affecting higher education.

Who is the fellowship intended for?

The programme is intended for postgraduate researchers. Applicants whose research interests relate to AI, higher education, digital education, emerging technologies, or related areas may find the opportunity particularly relevant.

When is the application deadline?

The application deadline is Monday, 14 September 2026.

Can researchers from outside one particular country apply?

The information provided for this announcement describes the programme as supporting DEC’s global research agenda, but it does not specify a particular nationality, country, race, or continent restriction in the information supplied here. Prospective applicants should therefore consult the official fellowship application information for the definitive eligibility and geographic requirements.

Conclusion

The Digital Education Council Postgraduate Research Fellowship 2026 offers postgraduate researchers an opportunity to become involved in an international research agenda focused on some of the most important issues facing higher education today. By supporting DEC’s global Working Groups and contributing to research publications on artificial intelligence and other emerging higher education issues, selected researchers can gain experience in collaborative and internationally oriented research. For postgraduate researchers interested in the intersection of AI, technology, digital education, research, and the future of higher education, the fellowship could be a valuable opportunity to expand their research experience and contribute to discussions shaping the next generation of education. Interested researchers should review the official application information carefully and ensure that their application is submitted by Monday, 14 September 2026.

item.content:encoded:
The Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship 2027 is offering an exceptional opportunity for eligible South African women seeking to pursue postgraduate studies at an international university. The scholarship is designed to support high-achieving postgraduate scholars who wish to undertake a Master’s or PhD programme abroad, providing full-cost funding for successful candidates.

According to the current Rhodes University postgraduate funding notice, applications for the 2027 scholarship are open from 24 August 2026 until 24 September 2026. Applicants are required to submit their application documents as a single PDF document to the designated Rhodes University contact.

The scholarship is administered through Rhodes University, which provides information on overseas study funding and postgraduate opportunities.

About the Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship

The Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship is a prestigious international postgraduate scholarship associated with Rhodes University and the Patrick and Margaret Flanagan Trust. Its purpose is to enable outstanding South African women graduates to pursue advanced postgraduate qualifications at universities outside South Africa.

The scholarship has a long history of supporting South African women to undertake postgraduate studies at leading international universities. Rhodes University has described it as a prestigious international scholarship intended to enable South African women graduates to obtain postgraduate qualifications overseas.

The scholarship has supported scholars across a wide range of academic disciplines. Historical records of recipients show that beneficiaries have undertaken Master’s and doctoral-level studies at international institutions, including universities in the United Kingdom and the United States.

Importantly, the scholarship is not limited to one specific academic discipline. Historical information about the award indicates that it has supported postgraduate study across different fields of academic and professional endeavour.

What Does the 2027 Scholarship Offer?

The 2027 announcement describes the Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship as providing full-cost funding for international Master’s and doctoral studies.

This makes the opportunity particularly valuable for applicants who have strong academic ambitions but may face financial barriers to pursuing postgraduate education at an overseas university.

Successful scholars can use the award to pursue full-time postgraduate studies at an international institution, subject to the terms and conditions of the scholarship.

Rather than simply providing a contribution toward tuition, the scholarship is presented as a full-cost funding opportunity. Applicants should, however, carefully review the official scholarship documentation and any award conditions before making financial or academic commitments.

Level of Study Supported

The scholarship is specifically intended for postgraduate-level study.

Eligible study levels include:

  • Master’s degree programmes
  • Doctoral or PhD programmes
  • Full-time postgraduate study at an international university

Applicants should therefore have a clear postgraduate academic plan and demonstrate why studying internationally is important to their academic, research, and professional development.

The scholarship’s historical record confirms that recipients have undertaken both Master’s and doctoral studies at overseas universities.

International Study Opportunity

One of the most attractive features of the Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship is the opportunity to undertake postgraduate studies outside South Africa.

The scholarship allows successful applicants to identify an international university that is appropriate for their intended course of study and research.

In the application, candidates are specifically asked to explain:

  1. Why they want to study at an international university.
  2. What they intend to do after completing their Master’s or PhD.
  3. Their intended research focus.
  4. Which university they intend to attend.
  5. Why they have selected that particular university.

This means applicants are expected to demonstrate that their proposed institution is not simply prestigious but also appropriate for their academic interests, research objectives, and long-term career plans.

Past scholarship recipients have studied at internationally recognised institutions. Rhodes University records, for example, document recipients undertaking postgraduate study at institutions including Oxford and Cambridge.

Who Can Apply for the Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship?

The current opportunity is intended for South African women pursuing postgraduate study overseas.

Rhodes University’s published information about previous recipients states that the scholarship aims to enable South African women graduates to attain postgraduate qualifications overseas.

Historical Rhodes University information also describes the scholarship as having been established specifically to support South African women scholars and notes that it was intended to give them opportunities to pursue postgraduate studies at leading international universities.

Eligibility at a Glance

Potential applicants should therefore be understood as:

  • Women applicants
  • South African citizens or women of South African descent, subject to the applicable scholarship terms
  • Applicants seeking postgraduate Master’s or PhD study
  • Candidates intending to study full-time at an international university
  • Strong academic performers with a compelling postgraduate or research plan
  • Applicants capable of demonstrating how their proposed international studies will contribute to their future academic, professional, or societal contribution

The available official material does not establish a separate racial quota or racial restriction. The key eligibility distinction identified in the scholarship’s published history is its focus on South African women. Earlier Rhodes University material describes the award as benefiting South African women scholars without restriction as to creed or colour.

Applicants should nevertheless consult the latest official application documentation because eligibility conditions can be updated.

Academic Background and Excellence

The scholarship is highly competitive and is aimed at academically strong candidates.

Previous Rhodes University information has described the award as being open to high-calibre applicants, with historical recipients demonstrating strong academic records. A Rhodes University report on a previous winner, for example, described the scholarship as being open to English-speaking South African postgraduate women with a first-class academic record.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their academic CV clearly communicates the following:

  • Previous university qualifications
  • Academic achievements
  • Research experience
  • Relevant academic awards
  • Publications, where applicable
  • Conference participation, where applicable
  • Research projects
  • Professional or academic leadership
  • Relevant work experience
  • Any other achievements demonstrating academic excellence and potential

Required Application Documents

For the 2027 application, Rhodes University requires applicants to submit a number of important documents.

All required materials should be combined into one single PDF document before submission.

The required application package includes the following.

1. Letter of Motivation

The motivation letter is one of the most important components of the application.

According to the official Rhodes University announcement, the motivation should address four central issues:

Why do you plan to study at an international university?

Applicants should explain why studying abroad is important to their academic and professional objectives.

Rather than simply stating that an overseas university is prestigious, applicants should explain the specific academic, research, institutional, or professional advantages that international study would provide.

For example, an applicant might discuss access to the following:

  • Specialised research facilities
  • Leading scholars in a particular field
  • Unique archives or datasets
  • Advanced laboratories
  • Specialised academic programmes
  • International research networks
  • Research methodologies unavailable or less accessible locally
  • Global professional networks
  • Collaborative opportunities

The strongest responses will connect the international study experience directly to the applicant’s research and long-term objectives.

2. Plans After Completing the Master’s or PhD

Applicants must explain what they intend to do after completing their postgraduate studies.

This section should demonstrate that the applicant has a clear vision for how the qualification will be used.

Potential areas to discuss include:

  • Returning to South Africa
  • Academic research
  • University teaching
  • Public service
  • Policy development
  • Professional practice
  • Entrepreneurship
  • Research and innovation
  • Community development
  • Institutional leadership
  • Knowledge transfer
  • Contribution to national development

Previous scholarship recipients have emphasised their intention to return to South Africa and apply the knowledge and skills gained abroad for the benefit of their country.

3. Intended Research Focus

Applicants should clearly explain what they intend to research.

A strong research focus should demonstrate:

  • A clearly defined topic
  • A significant research problem
  • Academic relevance
  • Potential societal or professional impact
  • Alignment with the proposed postgraduate programme
  • A realistic research direction
  • Why the selected international institution is particularly suitable

Applicants pursuing a PhD should pay particular attention to demonstrating the originality, relevance and potential contribution of their proposed research.

4. Proposed International University

Candidates must identify the university where they wish to study and explain why they have selected it.

The explanation should go beyond university rankings.

Applicants could consider discussing:

  • The university’s expertise in their field
  • Relevant professors or research groups
  • Research centres
  • Academic resources
  • Laboratories or specialised facilities
  • Institutional partnerships
  • Programme structure
  • Research environment
  • Availability of supervisors
  • International research networks
  • The institution’s relevance to the applicant’s career objectives

The goal is to demonstrate that there is a strong academic match between the applicant, the proposed programme and the university.

Detailed Academic CV

Applicants must provide a detailed academic CV.

The CV must also include the email contact details of three academic referees.

Importantly, one of the three academic referees must be a Head of Department or Dean.

Applicants should therefore select referees who are sufficiently familiar with their academic performance, research potential, intellectual abilities, and postgraduate ambitions.

A strong academic CV should clearly present the following:

  • Educational qualifications
  • Academic achievements
  • Research experience
  • Employment history, where relevant
  • Publications
  • Academic presentations
  • Conferences
  • Research projects
  • Scholarships and awards
  • Leadership activities
  • Professional memberships
  • Relevant technical or research skills
  • Academic referees

The CV should be carefully structured and tailored to demonstrate suitability for an internationally focused postgraduate scholarship.

Full Academic Transcript

Applicants are required to provide a full academic transcript.

The transcript must be certified.

Candidates should ensure that their transcript is complete and clearly shows their academic record.

Because the scholarship is highly competitive, applicants should also ensure that their academic achievements are clearly reflected in their motivation letter and CV rather than relying solely on the transcript to communicate their academic strengths.

Certified Identification Document

Applicants must also provide a certified copy of their ID or passport.

This document forms part of the formal application package and should therefore be prepared in advance.

Applicants should ensure that the copy is clear and properly certified according to the requirements applicable to their application.

How to Submit the Application

The application process requires candidates to combine all required documentation into one single PDF document.

The documents should not be sent as multiple separate attachments if following the published instructions.

The required application materials are:

  1. Letter of motivation
  2. Detailed academic CV
  3. Contact details for three academic referees
  4. Full certified academic transcript
  5. Certified ID or passport copy

The resulting PDF should be saved using the prescribed naming convention:

“Your Surname P&M Flanagan Scholarship Application”

The completed application should then be submitted to the designated Rhodes University contact at tasmin.jones@ru.ac.za.

Applicants should carefully check the official Rhodes University announcement and application documents before submitting their application because scholarship requirements may change.

APPLY HERE

Application Deadline

The application period for the Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship 2027 is

Opening date: 24 August 2026

Closing date: 24 September 2026

Applicants should not wait until the final day to submit their documents. Preparing a strong postgraduate scholarship application can take considerable time, particularly when applicants need to obtain certified academic documents and coordinate references.

The deadline is confirmed in the current Rhodes University overseas study funding announcement.

Why This Scholarship Is Highly Competitive

The Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship has a long-standing reputation for supporting high-achieving South African women pursuing postgraduate studies overseas.

Rhodes University has previously described the competition for the award as becoming increasingly difficult as the number and quality of applications increased.

This means that simply meeting the basic eligibility requirements may not be sufficient.

Applicants should aim to demonstrate a combination of:

  • Excellent academic performance
  • Strong intellectual potential
  • A clearly defined research agenda
  • A convincing reason for studying abroad
  • A carefully selected international university
  • Strong academic references
  • A realistic post-study career plan
  • Potential to contribute to South Africa
  • Evidence of leadership, initiative, or impact where applicable

How to Strengthen Your Application

1. Develop a compelling motivation

Your motivation should tell a coherent story.

Explain where you have come from academically, what you want to study, why you need to study it internationally, and what you intend to do with the knowledge afterwards.

Avoid generic statements such as “I have always wanted to study abroad.” Instead, explain precisely why the international institution and programme are important to your academic and research goals.

2. Demonstrate academic excellence

Use your CV and motivation letter to highlight your strongest academic achievements.

Where appropriate, demonstrate:

  • Outstanding grades
  • Research achievements
  • Academic awards
  • Publications
  • Conference presentations
  • Research assistantships
  • Academic leadership
  • Independent research experience

3. Explain the research problem clearly

If you are applying for Ph.D. study, your research focus should be particularly well developed.

Clearly communicate the problem you intend to investigate, why it matters, and what contribution your research could make.

4. Carefully justify your university choice

Do not select an institution simply because it is highly ranked.

Explain why the university is particularly suitable for your research.

If there is a relevant professor, research centre, laboratory, archive, programme or research group, explain how it connects to your proposed work.

5. Choose strong academic references

Your referees should be individuals who can provide meaningful evidence of your academic abilities and potential.

Because the application specifically requires three academic referees and one must be a Head of Department or Dean, candidates should contact their proposed referees well before the deadline.

6. Make your long-term contribution clear

Applicants should explain how the scholarship will contribute to their long-term career and how their postgraduate education will ultimately benefit South Africa.

A strong application should show that the candidate sees overseas study as a means of acquiring knowledge and expertise that can later be applied meaningfully.

What Makes the Scholarship Different?

The Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship stands out because it combines postgraduate academic support with an opportunity to study internationally.

It is particularly relevant for talented South African women who have reached the stage of pursuing advanced academic qualifications and want to gain exposure to international research and academic environments.

The historical record of the scholarship demonstrates that its beneficiaries have gone on to study at respected international universities and pursue careers across diverse academic and professional fields.

The scholarship has also supported scholars in different disciplines rather than restricting applicants to one specific subject area. Historical Rhodes University information indicates that postgraduate study could be pursued in any field of study.

Visit HERE for more information about the Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship 2027.

Important Note for Prospective Applicants

Applicants should distinguish between the general Rhodes University page listing overseas scholarships and the specific eligibility requirements of the Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship.

The current Rhodes University page presents the scholarship under its overseas study funding opportunities and provides the 2027 application dates and required documents.

However, the scholarship’s historical and recent Rhodes University materials identify it specifically as an opportunity for South African women.

Prospective applicants should therefore verify all current eligibility conditions in the official application documentation before preparing a submission.

Official Application Information

Applicants should use the official Rhodes University postgraduate funding page for the latest information, application instructions, and supporting documents.

Rhodes University – Overseas Study Funding and Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship 2027

The official Rhodes University page is particularly important because the university warns that scholarship providers may change information about their programmes without notice and advises applicants to check current scholarship information.

Conclusion

The Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship 2027 presents a significant opportunity for academically outstanding South African women seeking to pursue full-time Master’s or PhD studies at an international university.

With applications opening on 24 August 2026 and closing on 24 September 2026, prospective candidates have a limited period in which to prepare a competitive application.

The application requires more than academic qualifications. Candidates need to present a convincing case for international study, explain their intended research focus, identify an appropriate university, demonstrate their academic achievements, and provide a clear vision for what they intend to accomplish after completing their postgraduate studies.

Applicants should begin preparing early, particularly because the application requires a detailed academic CV, three academic referees, a certified academic transcript, and a certified identification document. The motivation letter should be carefully developed to demonstrate academic excellence, research potential, institutional fit, and a clear commitment to using the knowledge gained through international study.

For eligible South African women with strong academic records and ambitious postgraduate goals, the Patrick & Margaret Flanagan Scholarship could provide an important pathway to advanced international education, research exposure, and professional development.

item.content:encoded:
The AU-EU Youth Action Lab is launching its final Call for Proposals for youth-led initiatives seeking financial support to address global challenges in their communities. The programme supports young people and youth initiatives across Africa and Europe, providing funding designed to help turn innovative ideas, solutions, and advocacy efforts into practical action.

For the final cohort, eligible youth initiatives can apply for one of two grant opportunities: Innovation Grants or Entrepreneurship Grants. Both grant types are designed around a “powershifting” approach that places young people at the centre of decisions about the initiatives intended to benefit them.

The grants will support selected initiatives for 12 months, from January 2027 to December 2027.

Application deadline: 23 September 2026 at 13:00 Central African Time (CAT).

Important: Applicants can apply to only one of the two grant opportunities.

About the AU-EU Youth Action Lab

The AU-EU Youth Action Lab is focused on strengthening cooperation between young people in Africa and Europe. The programme creates opportunities for youth initiatives to connect with peers, exchange experiences, develop ideas, collaborate across contexts, and bring youth perspectives and solutions to decision-makers.

The initiative recognises the role young people can play in addressing major challenges within their communities and beyond.

Through its Youth Action Lab grants, the programme provides funding for youth-led initiatives that are developing solutions to global challenges or working to create more supportive environments for young people.

The final Call for Proposals is specifically open to eligible youth initiatives in selected African countries.

What Is the Purpose of the Youth Action Lab Grants?

The grants are designed to help young people move from ideas and advocacy to practical implementation.

The AU-EU Youth Action Lab is particularly interested in initiatives that can contribute to addressing global challenges within their own contexts.

Rather than simply providing conventional project funding, the programme describes its grant approach as “powershifting.”

This approach is built around three key principles:

1. Nothing About Youth Without Youth

Young people should have a meaningful role in decisions concerning youth initiatives.

To support this principle, a Youth Advisory Board of the Youth Action Lab will review and select proposals for funding.

This means the grant-selection process is designed to give young people a direct role in determining which initiatives receive support.

2. Organisational Capacity

The programme seeks to provide grants that do more than support individual activities.

According to the AU-EU Youth Action Lab, the funding aims to facilitate and nurture:

  • Organisational stability
  • Resilience
  • Financial security
  • Organisational capacity

This approach can help youth initiatives strengthen their ability to operate effectively and sustain their work.

3. Simplified Application and Reporting

The Youth Action Lab also aims to make its application and reporting processes appropriate for youth initiatives.

The programme emphasises application and reporting mechanisms that make sense for youth-led organisations and initiatives.

This is intended to reduce unnecessary complexity and make the funding process more accessible to the initiatives the programme seeks to support.

Two AU-EU Youth Action Lab Grant Opportunities

For the final Call for Proposals, the Youth Action Lab is offering two different types of grants.

Although each grant has a different focus, both are intended to support youth-led initiatives through the programme’s powershifting approach.

1. Innovation Grants

The Innovation Grants are designed to support youth initiatives that want to design, test and/or scale innovations linked to global challenges.

This grant category is particularly relevant to youth initiatives developing new approaches, ideas, models, tools, projects, or solutions to challenges affecting their communities.

An initiative may be at a stage where it is:

  • Designing a new solution;
  • Testing an existing idea;
  • Developing an innovative approach; or
  • Seeking to scale an innovation that has already demonstrated potential.

The central focus is on innovations connected to global challenges and their application within the initiative’s specific context.

Applicants interested in this funding stream should review the official Innovation Grants information before preparing their application.

Innovation Grants:
Find out more about Innovation Grants

2. Entrepreneurship Grants

The Entrepreneurship Grants are designed to support youth initiatives that advocate for an enabling environment for young entrepreneurs.

This grant type is therefore focused on initiatives working to improve the conditions in which young entrepreneurs can start, develop, and sustain their activities.

Potential applicants should review the specific requirements and focus of the Entrepreneurship Grants before deciding whether this is the most appropriate funding stream for their initiative.

Entrepreneurship Grants:
Find out more about Entrepreneurship Grants

Duration of the Grants

Each grant will run for 12 months.

The final cohort’s grant period is scheduled to run from:

January 2027 to December 2027

Selected initiatives will therefore have a full year to implement their supported activities within the grant period.

Applicants should take this timeframe into consideration when developing their project plans and determining what they realistically intend to accomplish during the funding period.

Eligible Countries

The final AU-EU Youth Action Lab Call for Proposals is open to eligible youth initiatives in the following countries:

  • Ethiopia
  • Kenya
  • Mozambique
  • Nigeria
  • Senegal
  • Sierra Leone
  • Somalia — Somaliland Region
  • Tanzania
  • Tunisia
  • Uganda
  • Zambia
  • Zimbabwe

Applicants should pay close attention to this geographical eligibility requirement because the supplied call specifically identifies these countries as eligible for the final cohort.

The source material does not indicate that applicants from countries outside this list are eligible for this particular call.

Who Can Apply?

The opportunity is intended for youth-led initiatives in the eligible countries.

The call describes its target audience broadly as young people and youth initiatives in their diversity that are working on solutions to global challenges or seeking to improve conditions for young entrepreneurs.

The information supplied does not provide a specific individual age range, nationality requirement, educational qualification, race requirement, or academic degree requirement.

Therefore, prospective applicants should consult the detailed requirements for their selected grant category before submitting an application.

The two available categories have different purposes:

  • Innovation Grants: For youth initiatives seeking to design, test, and/or scale innovations connected to global challenges.
  • Entrepreneurship Grants: For youth initiatives advocating for an enabling environment for young entrepreneurs.

What Makes These Grants Different?

One of the distinguishing features of the AU-EU Youth Action Lab grants is the programme’s emphasis on youth participation in decision-making.

The programme does not simply position young people as beneficiaries. Its powershifting approach is intended to give youth a meaningful role in shaping decisions about funding and initiatives.

The Youth Advisory Board’s involvement in reviewing and selecting proposals is an important example of this approach.

The programme also recognises that youth initiatives need more than short-term project financing. Its emphasis on organisational capacity means the grants are intended to contribute to the stability, resilience, financial security, and broader capacity of youth initiatives.

Potential Benefits of the AU-EU Youth Action Lab Grants

For successful youth initiatives, the grants can provide an opportunity to:

  • Obtain financial support for a youth-led initiative.
  • Develop, test, or scale innovative solutions to global challenges.
  • Support advocacy aimed at creating better conditions for young entrepreneurs.
  • Strengthen organisational capacity.
  • Improve organisational stability and resilience.
  • Contribute to financial security and sustainability.
  • Connect with youth initiatives and peers across Africa and Europe.
  • Share ideas and experiences with other young people.
  • Strengthen youth participation in decision-making.
  • Bring youth-led solutions and perspectives closer to decision-makers at African Union and European Union levels.
  • Implement a supported initiative over a 12-month period.

The exact funding amount and other grant-specific terms are not provided in the supplied information and should therefore be confirmed in the detailed information for the relevant grant category.

Application Deadline

The final deadline for applications is:

23 September 2026 at 13:00 Central African Time (CAT)

Applicants should submit their applications before the stated deadline.

Because the programme explicitly states that this is the final Call for Proposals, eligible initiatives should take the deadline seriously and avoid waiting until the final hours to complete their submissions.

Important Application Restriction

There is an important restriction that prospective applicants should understand before applying:

You can apply to only one grant opportunity at a time.

This means an initiative should carefully assess whether its project is better suited to the Innovation Grant or the Entrepreneurship Grant before submitting an application.

Applicants should not attempt to submit applications to both categories simultaneously.

How to Decide Which Grant Is Right for Your Initiative

The distinction between the two grant categories provides a useful starting point.

Choose the Innovation Grant if:

Your youth initiative is focused on developing, testing, or scaling an innovative solution connected to a global challenge.

For example, the initiative may involve developing a new approach, testing a solution in a particular community, or expanding an existing innovation.

Consider the Entrepreneurship Grant if:

Your initiative focuses on advocacy for an enabling environment for young entrepreneurs.

This could involve work aimed at improving the conditions, systems, policies, or support structures surrounding youth entrepreneurship.

Applicants should review the detailed requirements for each grant before making their final choice.

Application Support

The AU-EU Youth Action Lab provides an application guide for applicants who need assistance understanding how to submit their proposals.

Prospective applicants can consult the official guide:

AU-EU Youth Action Lab application guide

Applicants should use the official programme guidance to understand the application process and any specific requirements that apply to the selected grant category.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Although the supplied information does not provide a detailed scoring framework, applicants can prepare strategically by ensuring that their initiative clearly aligns with the purpose of the grant category they select.

1. Clearly Define the Problem

Explain the challenge your initiative is addressing and why it matters in your community or context.

2. Demonstrate Youth Leadership

Because the programme is specifically focused on youth-led initiatives, clearly explain how young people lead, design, implement, or make decisions within the initiative.

3. Choose the Correct Grant Category

Do not apply simply because a grant is available.

Determine whether your initiative genuinely fits the Innovation Grant or Entrepreneurship Grant.

4. Explain the Proposed Solution

Describe what your initiative intends to do, how it will work, and how it responds to the challenge you have identified.

5. Consider Sustainability

Think beyond the grant period. Explain how the initiative can strengthen organisational resilience, capacity, and longer-term impact.

6. Make the Project Realistic

The grant period lasts from January to December 2027. Applicants should therefore propose activities that can realistically be delivered during the 12-month period.

7. Demonstrate the Value of Your Approach

Explain what makes your initiative relevant, useful, innovative, or capable of contributing to meaningful change.

8. Follow the Application Instructions

Carefully review the official information and application guide before submitting. Make sure all required information is provided and that the application is submitted through the appropriate process.

Partnership Behind the AU-EU Youth Action Lab

The AU-EU Youth Action Lab is implemented through a consortium involving organisations including:

  • Oxfam
  • Restless Development
  • European Youth Forum

The programme’s website states that it has been prepared with financial assistance from the European Commission. It also notes that the views expressed by the consultants do not necessarily reflect the official opinion of the European Commission.

Final Call for Youth-Led Initiatives

This Call for Proposals represents the final cohort of the AU-EU Youth Action Lab grants.

The programme is therefore providing a significant opportunity for eligible youth initiatives to secure support for projects that address global challenges or strengthen the environment for young entrepreneurs.

With grants running for a full year from January to December 2027, successful applicants will have a defined period within which to implement their initiatives and pursue their intended objectives.

The powershifting approach is also central to the programme. By involving a Youth Advisory Board in proposal review and selection, emphasising organisational capacity, and simplifying application and reporting mechanisms, the programme seeks to create a funding process that is more responsive to youth initiatives.

Click HERE to learn more about the AU-EU Youth Action Lab Grants 2026.

Conclusion

The AU-EU Youth Action Lab Grants 2026 provide funding opportunities for youth-led initiatives in selected African countries that are working to address global challenges or promote a more enabling environment for young entrepreneurs.

For the final Call for Proposals, applicants can choose between two grant categories: Innovation Grants, which support initiatives developing, testing, or scaling innovations linked to global challenges, and Entrepreneurship Grants, which support initiatives advocating for an enabling environment for young entrepreneurs.

Both grant types will run for 12 months, from January to December 2027, and are built around the Youth Action Lab’s powershifting approach. This includes meaningful youth participation in funding decisions, a focus on organisational capacity, and simplified application and reporting processes.

The opportunity is open to eligible youth initiatives in Ethiopia, Kenya, Mozambique, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone, the Somaliland Region of Somalia, Tanzania, Tunisia, Uganda, Zambia, and Zimbabwe.

The final application deadline is 23 September 2026 at 13:00 Central African Time (CAT). Applicants must also remember that only one grant opportunity can be applied for at a time.

Youth-led initiatives that have an innovative solution to a global challenge or are working to create stronger conditions for young entrepreneurs should review the relevant grant requirements and begin preparing their application well before the deadline.

Visit the official AU-EU Youth Action Lab website

Discover more global Grant and African opportunities on OFY.

item.content:encoded:
UNICEF Thailand is accepting applications for its Young Professionals Programme (Communication) 2026, a structured early-career opportunity for university students and recent graduates who want practical experience in communications, digital advocacy, youth engagement, knowledge management, and children’s rights.

Based at the UNICEF Thailand Country Office in Bangkok, the programme gives selected Young Professionals the opportunity to work alongside experienced UNICEF colleagues while contributing to real communication and advocacy activities. Participants will gain hands-on exposure to the development and humanitarian sector, receive one-on-one guidance, strengthen professional skills, and build a portfolio through assignments connected to UNICEF’s work for children.

The programme is designed as a 4–6 month, part-time placement of approximately 15–20 hours per week, with flexible working arrangements intended to accommodate academic schedules.

UNICEF is looking particularly for third-year or above university students and recent graduates from relevant disciplines such as communications, social sciences, international relations, digital media, and related fields. Candidates should demonstrate an interest in children’s rights, development, or humanitarian work and need strong communication and writing skills in both Thai and English.

The application deadline is 3 September 2026, Southeast Asia Standard Time.

About UNICEF

UNICEF works in more than 190 countries and territories to protect children, defend their rights, support their development, and help them reach their full potential from early childhood through adolescence.

Its work covers areas including:

  • Child protection
  • Education
  • Health
  • Nutrition
  • Social policy
  • Humanitarian response
  • Advocacy
  • Communication
  • Youth participation

UNICEF emphasizes that promoting the rights of every child is central to its mission.

The organization also aims to provide professional and personal development opportunities for people working within its programmes, while maintaining an inclusive and multicultural working environment.

About UNICEF Thailand’s Young Professionals Programme

The UNICEF Thailand Young Professionals Programme is intended to give students from diverse academic backgrounds an opportunity to gain practical experience in the development and humanitarian sector.

Participants will work alongside UNICEF professionals and contribute directly to ongoing activities rather than participating only in classroom-style training.

The programme combines:

  • Practical assignments
  • Professional guidance
  • Mentorship
  • Exposure to UNICEF operations
  • Skills development
  • Career learning
  • Opportunities to contribute to children’s rights

The broader goal is to help young professionals understand how communications, advocacy, digital engagement, volunteer management, and knowledge-sharing activities are used to advance UNICEF’s mission.

Duration of the Programme

The placement lasts:

4 to 6 months

Participants are expected to work:

15 to 20 hours per week

The programme is:

Part-time

UNICEF states that working arrangements will be flexible in order to accommodate participants’ academic schedules.

This structure may be especially useful for current university students who want practical professional experience while continuing their studies.

Duty Station

The official duty station is:

Bangkok, Thailand

The opportunity is advertised through the UNICEF Thailand Country Office.

Although flexible working arrangements are mentioned, the posting does not describe the opportunity as a fully remote international programme. Applicants should therefore be prepared for the requirements associated with the Bangkok-based assignment.

Main Areas of Work

Participants may support UNICEF Thailand across four major areas:

  1. Digital content creation and publishing
  2. Digital advocacy and public campaigns
  3. Volunteer engagement
  4. Knowledge management and communication

These areas make the programme particularly relevant to students and recent graduates interested in communications, international development, media, advocacy, youth engagement, or public-interest campaigning.

1. Digital Content Creation and Publishing

Young Professionals may contribute to developing and publishing digital content for UNICEF platforms.

This can include content for:

  • Social media
  • UNICEF websites
  • Digital stories
  • Internal communication platforms
  • External communication channels

Participants may therefore gain practical exposure to how an international organization develops communication materials for different audiences.

This work can involve adapting messages to suit particular platforms while maintaining accuracy, clarity, and alignment with UNICEF’s communication standards.

Digital Communication Skills

The programme can help participants build experience in areas such as:

  • Digital storytelling
  • Social-media communication
  • Audience-focused messaging
  • Editorial preparation
  • Online publishing
  • Advocacy communication

Candidates with existing familiarity with social media and digital platforms may be especially well positioned to contribute.

2. Digital Advocacy and Public Campaigns

Participants will also support public advocacy campaigns.

Potential responsibilities include:

  • Participating in brainstorming sessions
  • Developing campaign ideas
  • Creating content
  • Recommending communication approaches
  • Suggesting techniques for reaching youth audiences
  • Supporting broader public engagement

This component can provide valuable insight into how UNICEF transforms children’s rights priorities into public-facing communication campaigns.

Reaching Youth Audiences

The programme places particular emphasis on communication with young people.

Participants may help UNICEF identify communication approaches that can make campaigns more relevant and accessible to youth audiences.

This could involve considering:

  • Platform choice
  • Tone
  • Format
  • Visual storytelling
  • Audience preferences
  • Participation
  • Digital engagement

Young Professionals can therefore bring their own perspectives as members of younger generations into UNICEF’s communication work.

3. Volunteer Engagement

The programme also includes responsibilities linked to the I Am UNICEF volunteer platform.

Participants may support:

  • Community management
  • Volunteer engagement
  • Youth activities
  • Event coordination
  • Communication with participants

This gives Young Professionals exposure not only to communications but also to community-building and volunteer engagement.

Supporting Youth and Volunteer Events

Participants may help facilitate administrative procedures connected with organizing and documenting:

  • Volunteer events
  • Youth events
  • Engagement activities

This may involve supporting logistical coordination, documentation, information management, or follow-up.

Candidates should therefore be comfortable working on both creative communication tasks and practical administrative responsibilities.

4. Knowledge Management and Knowledge Sharing

Knowledge management is another important component of the placement.

Participants may assist with:

  • Archive management
  • Organizing information
  • Knowledge sharing
  • Internal learning activities
  • Organizing sessions on different topics

Knowledge management helps organizations ensure that important information, experience, learning, and documentation remain accessible and usable.

For students interested in international organizations, this component can provide useful exposure to the behind-the-scenes systems that support programme continuity and institutional learning.

Learning and Development

UNICEF Thailand describes the Young Professionals Programme as an opportunity for participants to receive:

  • Hands-on mentorship
  • Exposure to UNICEF’s work
  • Practical professional experience
  • Opportunities to develop a portfolio
  • Experience contributing to high-impact initiatives

Participants will be able to work on projects reaching audiences in Thailand and potentially beyond.

This makes the programme more than an observational placement. Selected Young Professionals are expected to make meaningful contributions to ongoing work.

Certificate of Completion

Participants who successfully complete the programme will receive a:

Certificate of Completion from UNICEF

The certificate recognizes the participant’s contribution and experience during the programme.

This can be a useful addition to the professional profile of students and early-career applicants interested in:

  • United Nations careers
  • International development
  • Communication
  • Advocacy
  • NGOs
  • Humanitarian work
  • Public policy
  • International organizations

Who Can Apply?

Applicants should be:

  • Current university students in their third year or above, or
  • Recent university graduates

Relevant academic backgrounds may include:

  • Communications
  • Social sciences
  • International relations
  • Digital media
  • Related fields

The examples given are not necessarily exhaustive.

Applicants from other academic disciplines may still have relevant profiles if they can demonstrate strong alignment with the programme’s communication and children’s rights focus.

Interest in Children’s Rights

Candidates should demonstrate a genuine interest in:

  • Children’s rights
  • International development
  • Humanitarian work

This interest is important because the communication responsibilities are directly connected with UNICEF’s mandate.

Applicants should therefore avoid presenting themselves simply as people looking for general social-media experience.

A stronger application will explain why communication for children’s rights and social impact is meaningful to the candidate.

Thai and English Language Requirement

Applicants need:

Strong communication and writing skills in Thai and English

This is one of the most important practical eligibility requirements.

The programme involves communication activities in the Thailand Country Office, so candidates need to be comfortable creating and communicating information in both languages.

Applicants should make their language abilities clear in their CV and cover letter.

Digital Skills

Candidates should have familiarity with:

  • Digital platforms
  • Social media

UNICEF does not provide a long list of required software or technical programmes in the posting.

Applicants should therefore not assume advanced technical production skills are mandatory unless additional requirements appear in the application portal.

However, experience using social-media platforms, creating digital content, managing online communication, or supporting digital campaigns may strengthen an application.

Multicultural Working Environment

Candidates should demonstrate a willingness to:

  • Learn
  • Collaborate
  • Work with different perspectives
  • Operate in a multicultural environment

This is particularly relevant because UNICEF is an international organization whose personnel, partners, and programmes span diverse backgrounds and professional cultures.

UNICEF’s Core Values

Applicants are expected to align with UNICEF’s core values, summarized through the acronym CRITAS:

  • Care
  • Respect
  • Integrity
  • Trust
  • Accountability
  • Sustainability

These values guide how UNICEF expects personnel and participants to approach their work and relationships.

UNICEF Competencies

The posting identifies seven important competencies.

1. Builds and Maintains Partnerships

Participants should be able to develop respectful and productive relationships with colleagues and stakeholders.

2. Demonstrates Self-Awareness and Ethical Awareness

Candidates should demonstrate maturity, professionalism, and awareness of ethical responsibilities.

3. Drive to Achieve Results for Impact

UNICEF places emphasis on producing meaningful outcomes rather than simply completing tasks.

4. Innovates and Embraces Change

Communication environments evolve quickly.

Candidates should therefore be open to new ideas, technologies, platforms, and approaches.

5. Manages Ambiguity and Complexity

International development work can involve changing priorities and complex environments.

Participants should be adaptable.

6. Thinks and Acts Strategically

Even junior professionals should understand how individual communication activities connect with broader organizational objectives.

7. Works Collaboratively With Others

Teamwork is particularly important because participants will work closely with UNICEF Thailand colleagues.

UNICEF’s Work for Children

The posting emphasizes several fundamental rights that UNICEF works to protect.

Survival

Every child should have access to:

  • Basic healthcare
  • Peace
  • Security

Development

Children should have opportunities for:

  • Education
  • Adequate nutrition
  • Supportive homes
  • Healthy development

Protection

Children must be protected from:

  • Abuse
  • Neglect
  • Trafficking
  • Child labour
  • Exploitation

Participation

Children should have the opportunity to:

  • Express opinions
  • Be heard
  • Participate in decisions that affect them

Communication and advocacy play an important role in advancing all of these rights.

Application Requirements

Applicants are requested to submit:

  1. A CV
  2. A brief cover letter

The cover letter may be submitted in:

  • Thai, or
  • English

The application should be submitted through UNICEF’s official recruitment platform.

What to Include in Your CV

A strong CV should highlight:

  • Academic background
  • Current year of study or graduation date
  • Communications experience
  • Social-media experience
  • Digital content experience
  • Writing
  • Volunteer activities
  • Student leadership
  • Youth engagement
  • Development or humanitarian experience
  • Thai and English language skills

Applicants do not need years of professional employment to demonstrate relevance.

University projects, volunteering, student organizations, campaigns, publications, digital content, or relevant coursework may also help demonstrate suitable experience.

How to Write the Cover Letter

The cover letter is described as brief, so applicants should prioritize relevance.

A strong structure could address:

  1. Why you are interested in UNICEF Thailand
  2. Why children’s rights matter to you
  3. Your relevant communication or digital experience
  4. Your ability to work in Thai and English
  5. What you can contribute
  6. What you hope to learn

Avoid repeating your CV word for word.

Instead, use the cover letter to explain the connection between your experience and UNICEF’s communication work.

Application Deadline

The deadline is:

3 September 2026

The vacancy was advertised on:

20 August 2026

The official listing specifies the deadline according to Southeast Asia Standard Time.

Applicants should submit well before the closing time rather than waiting until the final hours.

How to Apply

Applications should be submitted through UNICEF’s official recruitment system.

Position: UNICEF Thailand – Young Professionals Programme (Communication)

Job Number: 595210

Duty Station: Bangkok, Thailand

Apply through UNICEF

Selection Process

Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted and invited to advance to the next stage of the recruitment process.

UNICEF may conduct:

  • Employment-history verification where applicable
  • Background checks

Selected candidates may also be asked to provide additional information during these procedures.

Safeguarding and Professional Conduct

This includes:

  • Sexual harassment
  • Abuse of authority
  • Discrimination

UNICEF also applies strict child-safeguarding principles.

All selected candidates are expected to comply fully with these standards.

Diversity and Inclusion

UNICEF states that its workforce should reflect the diversity of the children and communities it serves.

The organization emphasizes inclusion regardless of characteristics including:

  • Race or ethnicity
  • Age
  • Disability
  • Gender identity
  • Sexual orientation
  • Religion
  • Nationality
  • Socio-economic background

UNICEF also provides reasonable accommodation for candidates with disabilities during the recruitment process and, where appropriate, during assignments.

Visa and Health Insurance

The vacancy contains standard UNICEF language stating that selected candidates are responsible for ensuring that any required:

  • Visa
  • Health insurance

remain valid for the assignment period where applicable.

Applicants who are not already able to work or reside in Thailand should therefore pay particular attention to immigration and insurance requirements.

The posting does not state that UNICEF will provide visa sponsorship for this programme.

Is the Programme Paid?

The supplied vacancy information does not state a stipend, salary, or financial allowance for the Young Professionals Programme.
