The clearly stated benefits relate primarily to:

  • Social-media accounts
  • Student organizations
  • Communication assignments
  • Photography
  • Video
  • Writing

2. Demonstrate Both Thai and English

Because both languages are explicitly required, mention them prominently.

Where relevant, include examples showing that you have written or created content in both languages.

3. Connect Communication With Children’s Rights

UNICEF is not simply recruiting a social-media intern.

Your application should demonstrate why communication can be used to advance:

  • Children’s rights
  • Advocacy
  • Youth engagement
  • Social development

4. Show Digital Awareness

Be ready to explain how younger audiences consume information and how organizations can communicate effectively with them.

5. Demonstrate Creativity

The role includes brainstorming and content creation.

Examples of projects where you generated original communication ideas can strengthen your profile.

6. Highlight Youth or Volunteer Engagement

Experience working with:

  • Youth groups
  • Volunteer networks
  • Student organizations
  • Community initiatives

may be particularly relevant to the I Am UNICEF responsibilities.

7. Keep the Cover Letter Brief and Specific

A focused letter tailored to UNICEF Thailand will be stronger than a generic UN application letter.

item.content:encoded:
JPMorgan Chase is inviting qualified university students to apply for its 2027 Corporate Analyst Development Program – Summer Analyst, a nine-week internship designed for students who want to develop practical business, analytics, project management and process improvement skills within one of the world’s leading financial institutions.

The opportunity is based in the United States, with positions available in Newark, Delaware; Plano, Texas; and Tampa, Florida. The role falls under JPMorgan Chase’s Corporate Sector and is classified as a Seasonal Employee position. The job identification number is 210765772.

The program is particularly suited to students who enjoy working with data, solving complex problems, improving business processes and collaborating across teams. Unlike front-office, client-facing or software engineering positions, the Corporate Analyst Development Program focuses on the internal business capabilities that help large organizations operate effectively and make informed decisions.

About the JPMorgan Chase Summer Analyst Program

The JPMorgan Chase Corporate Analyst Development Program Summer Analyst position provides students with an opportunity to gain hands-on professional experience through meaningful projects that can influence real business outcomes.

During the nine-week internship, Summer Analysts will work on initiatives involving areas such as process improvement, strategic decision-making, analytics and project delivery. Participants will collaborate with different teams, interact with senior stakeholders and gain a broader understanding of how various parts of a global financial institution operate.

The program also introduces participants to modern approaches to business decision-making, including the responsible use of data, analytics, emerging technologies and artificial intelligence. This makes the opportunity relevant to students seeking to build transferable skills that can be applied across different professional environments.

Three Core Areas of Development

A central feature of the Corporate Analyst Development Program is its focus on three core disciplines:

  1. Analytics
  2. Project Management
  3. Process Improvement

Through these areas, interns can develop a broad understanding of how organizations use information, people, processes and technology to address business challenges.

1. Analytics

The analytics component focuses on using data to generate useful business insights.

Summer Analysts may be involved in:

  • Exploring data to identify trends, patterns and opportunities.
  • Translating analytical findings into clear and actionable recommendations.
  • Supporting business decision-making through structured problem-solving.
  • Using modern and AI-enabled tools to accelerate insight generation.

This area is particularly relevant for students who enjoy interpreting information, identifying patterns and using evidence to support decisions.

2. Project Management

The project management component focuses on helping turn ideas and business priorities into practical execution.

Responsibilities may include:

  • Supporting projects that advance business priorities.
  • Coordinating activities across different teams.
  • Keeping projects on track and aligned with objectives.
  • Identifying risks and helping resolve problems.
  • Adapting to changing priorities.
  • Communicating project updates clearly to stakeholders at different levels.

Students interested in organization, coordination, leadership and delivering projects can therefore find this area particularly valuable.

3. Process Improvement

The process improvement component focuses on examining existing workflows and identifying ways to make them more efficient and effective.

Summer Analysts may:

  • Analyze workflows to identify inefficiencies.
  • Identify opportunities to improve processes and systems.
  • Use data to understand the root causes of problems.
  • Support initiatives designed to improve ways of working.
  • Help implement changes that produce sustainable and measurable results.

This area is suitable for students who enjoy identifying problems, simplifying complex processes and developing practical solutions.

Who Should Apply?

The JPMorgan Chase Corporate Analyst Development Program is aimed at students who are academically progressing toward graduation while demonstrating the ability to think critically, communicate effectively and work collaboratively.

Applicants must be pursuing a Bachelor of Arts, Bachelor of Science, or fifth-year Master of Arts/Master of Science degree, with an expected graduation date of December 2027 or June 2028.

Candidates should also demonstrate:

  • Strong analytical abilities.
  • Critical-thinking and problem-solving skills.
  • The ability to synthesize complex information.
  • The ability to translate data into actionable insights.
  • An interest in data, analytics, artificial intelligence and emerging technologies.
  • A digital-first mindset.
  • Leadership demonstrated through academic, extracurricular or professional activities.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
  • The ability to collaborate and influence across teams.
  • Initiative and a proactive approach to work.
  • A team-oriented attitude.
  • A willingness to take ownership of responsibilities.
  • Curiosity and a growth mindset.
  • Strong learning agility.
  • The ability to adapt to a fast-changing environment.
  • Familiarity with Microsoft Office and business tools.

Preferred Academic Qualification

Although the program lists the qualifications above as required, JPMorganChase identifies a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.2 on a 4.0 scale as a preferred qualification.

U.S. Work Authorization Requirement

One of the most important eligibility conditions is that applicants must be authorized to work in the United States.

JPMorgan Chase explicitly states that it does not provide employment-based immigration sponsorship for this program. The company also states that it will not provide assistance or documentation supporting other forms of immigration sponsorship or benefits, including Optional Practical Training (OPT) or Curricular Practical Training (CPT).

Applicants should therefore carefully assess their work authorization status before applying.

The company further notes that performance during the internship will be evaluated when considering candidates for potential full-time opportunities after graduation, and the resulting full-time role is also ineligible for employment-based immigration sponsorship.

Internship Locations

The 2027 Summer Analyst opportunity is available in three U.S. locations:

  • Newark, Delaware
  • Plano, Texas
  • Tampa, Florida

Applicants are required to provide a location preference as part of their application.

Potential Pathway to Full-Time Employment

The internship can also serve as an important pathway for high-performing participants.

According to JPMorgan Chase, successful Summer Analysts may receive an offer to return for its full-time Corporate Analyst Development Program, which is a two-year rotational experience across the three core disciplines of Analytics, Project Management and Process Improvement.

This means the internship is not limited to short-term exposure. For strong performers, it can potentially lead to continued professional development within the organization following graduation.

Application Process

JPMorgan Chase outlines a multi-stage application process for candidates interested in the Corporate Analyst Development Program.

Step 1: Submit the Application

Applicants must submit a complete and thoughtful application, including their resume and location preference.

The company advises candidates to complete all relevant application questions carefully because the application and resume provide the recruiting team with an initial understanding of the applicant’s background and suitability for the program.

Step 2: Complete the HireVue Interview

Candidates who meet the minimum application criteria will receive an invitation to complete a video interview powered by HireVue.

This stage provides applicants with an opportunity to expand on their resume and demonstrate their experiences to the recruiting team and hiring managers.

The HireVue stage is required. JPMorgan Chase states that an application will not proceed to further review until this step has been completed. Applicants are strongly encouraged to complete their video interview within three days of receiving the invitation.

Step 3: Rolling Application Review

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

Because the program may close once positions are filled, JPMorganChase strongly encourages interested candidates to submit their applications as early as possible rather than waiting until the stated deadline.

Important Application Details

The key information for prospective applicants includes:

  • Organization: JPMorgan Chase
  • Program: 2027 Corporate Analyst Development Program – Summer Analyst
  • Job Identification: 210765772
  • Opportunity Type: Summer internship
  • Business Unit: Corporate Sector
  • Job Category: Seasonal Employee
  • Duration: Nine weeks
  • Locations: Newark, DE; Plano, TX; Tampa, FL
  • Schedule: Full-time
  • Expected Graduation: December 2027 or June 2028
  • Preferred GPA: 3.2/4.0
  • Work Authorization: Authorization to work in the United States required
  • Immigration Sponsorship: Not provided
  • Application Deadline: December 1, 2026, at 8:00 AM
  • Application Review: Rolling basis

What Candidates Should Emphasize in Their Applications

Given the requirements of the position, applicants should ensure that their resumes and application responses clearly demonstrate evidence of analytical thinking, problem-solving, leadership, communication and teamwork.

Relevant experiences may come from academic projects, extracurricular activities, student leadership, previous internships, employment or other professional experiences. JPMorgan Chase specifically recognizes leadership demonstrated through academic, extracurricular or professional activities.

Applicants should also make their interest in data, analytics, AI, and emerging technologies clear, particularly where they can demonstrate how they have used technology or data to understand a problem, improve a process or support a decision.

Because the program includes Analytics, Project Management and Process Improvement, candidates can also demonstrate experiences involving project coordination, workflow improvement, data analysis, research, process optimization and cross-team collaboration.

About JPMorgan Chase

JPMorgan Chase describes itself as one of the world’s oldest financial institutions, with a history spanning more than 200 years. The organization provides financial solutions to consumers, small businesses and major corporate, institutional and government clients through the J.P. Morgan and Chase brands. Its activities include investment banking, consumer and small business banking, commercial banking, financial transaction processing and asset management.

The company’s Corporate Functions cover areas including finance, risk, human resources and marketing. According to JPMorgan Chase, these corporate teams play an important role in supporting the company’s businesses, clients, customers and employees.

Equal Opportunity and Inclusion

JPMorgan Chase states that it is committed to an inclusive work environment and values the different skills, backgrounds and professional experiences of its workforce.

The company states that it does not discriminate on the basis of protected attributes, including race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital or veteran status, pregnancy or disability, among other characteristics protected by applicable law. It also states that reasonable accommodations are available for applicants and employees with disabilities.

Application Deadline

The official application deadline listed for the 2027 Corporate Analyst Development Program—Summer Analyst is

December 1, 2026, at 8:00 AM.

However, candidates should not necessarily wait until the deadline. JPMorgan Chase states that applications are reviewed on a rolling basis and that programs may close once available positions have been filled. Early application is therefore strongly encouraged.

APPLY HERE

How to Apply

Interested candidates should prepare a complete application, including an updated resume and location preference, and submit it through the official JPMorganChase careers platform.

The application should accurately demonstrate the candidate’s academic background, leadership experience, analytical abilities, communication skills, interest in technology and ability to work collaboratively. Candidates who progress beyond the initial screening should also be prepared to complete the required HireVue video interview.

Visit HERE for more information about the JPMorgan Chase 2027 Corporate Analyst Development Program.

Conclusion

The JPMorgan Chase 2027 Corporate Analyst Development Program—Summer Analyst offers eligible university students a structured nine-week opportunity to gain practical experience in analytics, project management and process improvement.

With placements available in Newark, Delaware; Plano, Texas; and Tampa, Florida, the program provides exposure to meaningful business projects, senior stakeholders, cross-functional collaboration, data-driven decision-making, and emerging technologies. High-performing participants may also have an opportunity to continue into JPMorgan Chase’s two-year, full-time rotational Corporate Analyst Development Program after graduation.

Students who meet the academic requirements, demonstrate strong analytical and interpersonal abilities, and are authorized to work in the United States should consider applying early. Since applications are reviewed on a rolling basis and the program may close once positions are filled, submitting a strong application before the December 1, 2026, 8:00 AM deadline is important.

For more global Internship opportunities, visit OFY HERE.

item.content:encoded:
Are you an aspiring researcher in computer science, artificial intelligence, data science, mathematics, physics, statistics, or electrical engineering looking for a fully funded PhD opportunity in Europe? The Institute for Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence and Technology (INSAIT) in Sofia, Bulgaria, is offering talented doctoral candidates the opportunity to pursue a world-class PhD while receiving a full doctoral fellowship of €39,684 gross per year.

The INSAIT PhD programme is designed for ambitious students who want to develop into independent scientists, researchers, technology leaders, and deep-tech innovators. Successful candidates work closely with leading researchers from INSAIT and affiliated international institutions, while undertaking advanced research in computer science and artificial intelligence.

Unlike many scholarship programmes that have a fixed annual deadline, INSAIT uses a rolling admission process, meaning prospective doctoral candidates can submit applications throughout the year.

Opportunity Overview

  • Opportunity: PhD at INSAIT
  • Category: Scholarship / Fully Funded PhD Fellowship
  • Host Institution: INSAIT – Institute for Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence and Technology
  • Location: Sofia, Bulgaria
  • Study Level: Doctoral / PhD
  • Fields: Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Mathematics, Physics, Statistics and Electrical Engineering
  • Funding: €39,684 gross per year
  • Programme Duration: Up to 5 years
  • Application System: Rolling admissions
  • Deadline: No fixed deadline; applications are accepted throughout the year
  • Language: English
  • Degree Issuing Institution: INSAIT at Sofia University “St. Kliment Ohridski”
  • Eligible Applicants: International applicants are welcome

About INSAIT

INSAIT is the Institute for Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence and Technology, located in Sofia, Bulgaria. The institute was established in 2022 in partnership with leading technical universities including ETH Zurich and EPFL and operates as a special unit of Sofia University “St. Kliment Ohridski.” Its mission is to build a world-class research and education environment focused on computer science, artificial intelligence and related technologies.

The institute aims to attract outstanding researchers and train the next generation of scientists and technology leaders. Its research ecosystem has connections with internationally recognized academic and technology institutions, making the PhD programme particularly attractive to candidates seeking international research exposure.

For doctoral candidates, the programme goes beyond classroom-based education. Students are expected to become active researchers, work with experienced advisers, contribute to high-quality research and develop the expertise necessary to pursue careers in academia, industry, entrepreneurship and advanced research laboratories.

What Does the INSAIT PhD Fellowship Offer?

One of the most significant features of the programme is its financial support.

All admitted doctoral candidates receive a full PhD fellowship worth €39,684 gross per year. This financial support is intended to allow students to concentrate fully on their doctoral research rather than having to seek unrelated employment to finance their studies.

INSAIT also notes that doctoral fellowships may be available through major technology companies, including DeepMind and Amazon Web Services.

The fellowship therefore provides an opportunity for qualified researchers to pursue advanced doctoral studies while receiving substantial financial support.

Key financial benefit

  • €39,684 gross per year
  • Full doctoral fellowship for admitted candidates
  • Financial support can continue during the first two years for candidates who enter with a Bachelor’s degree and complete their Master’s degree within the programme
  • Students are expected to dedicate themselves full-time to doctoral research
  • There is no requirement to repay the fellowship if a candidate ultimately fails the doctoral programme, according to INSAIT’s FAQ.

It is important to understand that the stated amount is gross, rather than net, meaning the amount received after applicable taxes or deductions may be lower.

Who Is Eligible for the INSAIT PhD?

INSAIT is looking for talented candidates with strong academic backgrounds who have obtained, or will have obtained by the time they begin the doctoral programme, a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree.

The institute generally considers applicants with academic backgrounds in:

  • Computer Science
  • Data Science
  • Mathematics
  • Physics
  • Statistics
  • Electrical Engineering

Candidates who are currently completing their Bachelor’s or Master’s degrees may also be considered, provided they obtain the relevant degree before beginning the doctoral programme. Recent Bachelor’s and Master’s graduates are therefore encouraged to apply if they meet the academic requirements.

Applicants with only a Bachelor’s degree

An important feature of the programme is that applicants do not necessarily need to already hold a Master’s degree.

A candidate who has a Bachelor’s degree but does not yet have an MSc can be admitted with the expectation that they will complete their Master’s degree during the first two years of the INSAIT doctoral programme.

During this period, the student remains financially supported through the €39,684 gross annual fellowship and is expected to continue toward the second part of the PhD programme if successful.

This makes the opportunity particularly interesting for outstanding Bachelor’s graduates who want to move directly into an advanced research environment.

Are International Students Eligible?

Yes. International applicants are explicitly welcome.

INSAIT states that it aims to become an international, world-class research and education institution and embraces diversity. English is the working language, and communications within the programme take place in English.

Therefore, the programme is not restricted to Bulgarian citizens.

Qualified candidates from Africa, Asia, Europe, North America, South America, Oceania and other parts of the world can be considered, provided they meet the academic and programme requirements.

For international candidates, however, immigration requirements should be considered. INSAIT notes that visa applications and work-permit procedures can sometimes affect the timing of a student’s start date.

What Research Areas Can PhD Students Pursue?

Applicants do not necessarily have to commit to one highly specific PhD research topic before submitting their application.

INSAIT allows candidates to identify several areas of interest. Students are encouraged to have a general idea of the research directions they would like to explore, but their interests can evolve during the programme.

The institute also encourages interdisciplinary research and collaboration, meaning a final PhD topic may combine several areas of computer science, artificial intelligence, mathematics or related disciplines.

This approach is particularly useful for candidates who have strong technical interests but are still exploring the precise research problem they want to investigate.

How Long Is the INSAIT PhD Programme?

The doctoral programme can last up to five years and is divided into two major stages.

Part I: Up to two years

During the first part, the student works on research with their adviser while exploring potential research directions.

The objective is to develop sufficient expertise and research understanding to formulate a specific PhD thesis topic.

By the end of this stage, the candidate is expected to define the theme of their doctoral research and defend it before an INSAIT graduate committee.

The first two years are not necessarily limited to one research topic. Students are encouraged to gain exposure to multiple areas and collaborate with other researchers.

Part II: Up to three years

After successfully completing the first stage, the student proceeds to the second part of the programme.

The focus then becomes deeper research into the selected thesis topic, with the objective of producing significant and original research results.

INSAIT explains that, as a rule of thumb, a PhD thesis should be based on at least three publications in top academic venues. However, the final thesis should form a coherent body of academic work rather than simply being a collection of previously published papers.

Students are also expected to contribute to the broader research environment by collaborating with other doctoral researchers and potentially supervising or working with Master’s students.

World-Class Mentorship and Research Supervision

A major advantage of the INSAIT PhD is access to experienced researchers and international mentors.

Students are mentored by INSAIT faculty members as well as affiliated mentors. The institute’s broader research network includes researchers associated with leading institutions around the world.

For students who are supervised primarily by an external adviser, INSAIT has a structure designed to facilitate close collaboration with the adviser’s research group.

An externally supervised student may spend approximately three months per year visiting the adviser’s institution. According to INSAIT, these visits are fully covered by the institute.

The arrangement can allow students to work directly with established research groups while maintaining their connection to INSAIT.

External advisers are also expected to visit INSAIT several times per year and provide regular technical guidance to their doctoral students.

This international supervision model can provide doctoral students with exposure to different research environments and international academic networks.

Who Issues the PhD Degree?

INSAIT is legally part of Sofia University “St. Kliment Ohridski.”

Consequently, the official doctoral degree is issued by INSAIT at Sofia University.

This means students are participating in INSAIT’s specialized research environment while the degree is institutionally connected to Sofia University.

Required Application Documents

Candidates should prepare a strong application package before applying.

The main documents requested by INSAIT include the following.

1. Curriculum Vitae

Applicants should provide a detailed academic and professional CV.

The CV should highlight:

  • Universities attended
  • Degrees obtained or currently being completed
  • Academic achievements
  • Relevant professional experience
  • Research experience
  • Publications, where applicable
  • Technical achievements
  • Extracurricular achievements
  • Awards and distinctions
  • Other accomplishments relevant to doctoral research

For a competitive PhD application, candidates should ensure that the CV demonstrates evidence of research potential rather than simply listing educational qualifications.

2. Degree Certificates

Applicants who have already graduated should submit official copies of their Bachelor’s and/or Master’s degree certificates.

Candidates still completing their degrees should ensure that their graduation timeline is compatible with the expected start of the doctoral programme.

3. University Transcripts

Applicants must provide official university transcripts showing their academic coursework, academic hours and grades.

Strong academic performance can be important because INSAIT evaluates the quality of a candidate’s coursework and grades as part of the admissions process.

4. Recommendation Letters

Recommendation letters are listed as optional, but candidates can submit two letters from individuals who can attest to their academic and scientific achievements.

Ideally, referees should be able to provide meaningful evidence of the applicant’s:

  • Research ability
  • Academic performance
  • Technical skills
  • Intellectual curiosity
  • Problem-solving ability
  • Independence
  • Potential for doctoral research

Recommendation letters should include the full contact details of the recommender.

5. Motivation Letter

The motivation letter is an important component of the application.

Candidates should clearly explain:

  • Why they want to pursue a PhD
  • Why they are interested in INSAIT
  • Their general research interests
  • Their academic and research objectives
  • Their long-term goals
  • Relevant experiences or achievements
  • Why INSAIT’s research environment is appropriate for their ambitions

INSAIT recommends that the motivation statement generally be no more than two A4 pages.

6. English Language Proficiency

Applicants are expected to have a strong command of English.

Where available, candidates can provide formal evidence of English-language proficiency, such as:

  • IELTS
  • TOEFL
  • Cambridge English qualifications
  • Other recognized English-language certificates

INSAIT’s working language is English, so candidates should be comfortable conducting academic communication and research in English.

Important Document Requirement

All application documents must either be issued in English or translated into English.

Applicants should therefore make sure that documents originally issued in another language are accompanied by appropriate English translations.

INSAIT also explains that official documents are accepted for initial admission, but documentation may need to be legalized when the doctoral contract is issued.

How Is the Application Assessed?

INSAIT evaluates applicants based on several factors rather than relying on one qualification alone.

The assessment may consider:

  1. Academic qualifications
  2. Quality of university coursework
  3. Academic grades
  4. Extracurricular achievements
  5. Motivation
  6. Recommendation letters
  7. Research potential
  8. Alignment with the institute’s research interests
  9. Performance during technical assessments or interviews

Strong grades can help demonstrate academic preparation, but applicants should also use their CV and motivation letter to show evidence of curiosity, technical ability and research potential.

Technical Interview

Candidates who successfully progress through the initial assessment may be invited to a technical interview.

The interview may be conducted by the faculty member or members who are interested in the candidate’s profile.

This stage provides the research group with an opportunity to assess the candidate’s technical preparation, research interests and suitability for doctoral-level work.

Applicants should therefore be prepared to discuss their academic background, technical knowledge, previous projects, research interests and reasons for applying to INSAIT.

When Will Applicants Receive a Decision?

INSAIT states that applicants should receive notification of the application result within two months of applying.

If an adviser or several advisers are interested in the candidate, the applicant may be contacted for further steps, including technical interviews and assessments.

Successful progression can ultimately result in a working PhD contract.

Is There an Application Deadline?

There is no fixed annual deadline for the INSAIT PhD programme.

INSAIT uses a rolling admissions process, allowing candidates to apply at any point during the year.

Deadline: Rolling Admissions

Because applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, prospective applicants should not interpret the absence of a fixed deadline as a reason to delay.

Candidates should apply when they have a strong application package ready, particularly because the programme is competitive and applicants may be contacted by potential advisers after submission.

What Happens If You Are Admitted?

Successful candidates can expect to begin the doctoral programme as soon as possible, subject to the relevant administrative requirements.

For international students, visa and work-permit procedures can affect the start date.

Once the doctoral programme begins, students are expected to dedicate themselves fully to research at INSAIT.

The programme specifically requires PhD students to be 100% focused on their doctoral research and not work other jobs alongside their studies.

Career Opportunities After the PhD

The INSAIT PhD is designed not only to award a doctoral degree but also to prepare students for high-level careers in research and technology.

According to INSAIT, graduates may pursue opportunities including:

  • University research and academic careers
  • Professorships
  • Research scientist positions
  • Artificial intelligence research
  • Big-tech research laboratories
  • Industrial research and development
  • Engineering R&D departments
  • Deep-tech entrepreneurship
  • Technology startups
  • International research collaborations

Potential employers and research environments mentioned by INSAIT include major technology and research organizations such as DeepMind, Google Brain, Microsoft Research and Amazon, among others.

For candidates interested in becoming research scientists or technology entrepreneurs, the combination of advanced research, international mentorship and industry connections can provide a strong foundation for future career development.

Why This PhD Opportunity Stands Out

There are several reasons qualified candidates may want to consider the INSAIT doctoral programme.

1. Full financial support

The €39,684 gross annual fellowship provides substantial financial support throughout the doctoral programme.

2. International research environment

International applicants are welcome, and English is the working language.

3. Strong academic mentorship

Students have access to INSAIT faculty and affiliated international mentors.

4. Flexible research direction

Students can explore several research areas before settling on a final PhD topic.

5. International research exposure

Students working with external advisers may have opportunities to spend approximately three months per year at the adviser’s institution, with visits covered by INSAIT.

6. Five-year programme structure

The programme allows up to five years for exploration, thesis development and advanced research.

7. Opportunity for Bachelor’s graduates

Applicants who have only a Bachelor’s degree can potentially enter the doctoral programme and complete a Master’s degree during the first two years.

8. Strong career potential

The programme is designed to prepare graduates for academic careers, research laboratories, startups and industrial R&D.

How to Apply for the INSAIT PhD

Interested candidates should first review the official PhD programme information and identify the research areas that align with their academic and professional interests.

Applicants should then prepare their application documents, including their CV, academic records, degree certificates where applicable, motivation letter and supporting recommendation letters.

The application is submitted through INSAIT’s online recruitment platform.

Candidates who encounter difficulties accessing the application platform can contact INSAIT through the contact details provided on the official programme page.

APPLY HERE

How to Make Your Application More Competitive

Although there is no single formula for gaining admission, prospective candidates can take several practical steps to strengthen their applications.

Demonstrate academic strength

Highlight courses and academic projects that are directly relevant to your intended research area.

For example, applicants interested in machine learning could emphasize coursework in:

  • Algorithms
  • Linear algebra
  • Probability
  • Statistics
  • Optimization
  • Machine learning
  • Artificial intelligence
  • Programming

Highlight research experience

Research experience can help distinguish an applicant from candidates who have only completed coursework.

Include:

  • Research projects
  • Undergraduate or Master’s theses
  • Publications
  • Preprints
  • Research internships
  • Technical projects
  • Open-source contributions
  • Conference participation
  • Laboratory experience

Write a targeted motivation letter

Avoid submitting a generic statement that could be sent to any university.

Explain specifically why INSAIT’s research environment appeals to you and identify broad research areas that interest you.

Your statement should connect your previous experience, current interests and future research ambitions.

Choose recommenders carefully

If submitting recommendation letters, choose people who know your academic or research capabilities well.

A detailed letter from someone who has directly supervised your research can generally provide more meaningful evidence than a generic letter from someone who knows you only superficially.

Prepare for technical interviews

Candidates who progress to the interview stage should be prepared to explain their previous projects and demonstrate their technical understanding.

Review the fundamentals relevant to your intended research area and be ready to discuss why particular research problems interest you.

Visit HERE to learn more about the PhD at INSAIT in Bulgaria.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I apply if I have not yet completed my Master’s degree?

Yes. INSAIT can consider applicants who have a Bachelor’s degree but not a Master’s degree. Such students are expected to complete the Master’s degree during the first two years of the doctoral programme.

Can international students apply?

Yes. INSAIT explicitly welcomes international applicants and conducts its academic communication in English.

Do I need to choose my exact PhD topic before applying?

No. Candidates can identify several areas of interest, and their research interests may evolve during the programme. INSAIT also encourages interdisciplinary research.

Is the fellowship fully funded?

Admitted candidates receive a full doctoral fellowship of €39,684 gross per year.

How long does the PhD take?

The programme can last up to five years, divided into an initial period of up to two years and a second period of up to three years.

Is the PhD full-time?

Yes. Students are expected to be fully focused on their doctoral research and not hold other jobs during the programme.

Does INSAIT have a fixed application deadline?

No. The programme operates on a rolling admissions basis, so applications can be submitted throughout the year.

When will I receive an application decision?

INSAIT states that applicants will be notified within two months of applying.

What language are the studies conducted in?

English is the working language at INSAIT, and communications take place in English.

Is it necessary to legalize documents?

Official documents are accepted for initial acceptance, but documentation may need to be legalized when the doctoral contract is issued.

What happens if I fail the doctoral programme?

According to INSAIT’s published FAQ, candidates are not required to repay the salary or fellowship they received before failing the programme.

Conclusion

The INSAIT PhD programme in Bulgaria represents a significant opportunity for ambitious researchers seeking fully funded doctoral study in computer science, artificial intelligence and related technical disciplines.

With a €39,684 gross annual doctoral fellowship, a programme lasting up to five years, international mentorship, opportunities for collaboration with leading research groups and an English-language research environment, the programme is particularly suited to candidates who want to build careers in advanced research, academia, artificial intelligence, deep technology or technology entrepreneurship.

The absence of a fixed annual deadline is another important advantage because INSAIT uses rolling admissions and allows qualified candidates to apply throughout the year. However, prospective applicants should still prepare carefully and submit a strong application rather than waiting unnecessarily.

For candidates with a strong background in computer science, mathematics, data science, physics, statistics or electrical engineering, this programme could provide the financial support, mentorship and international research exposure needed to progress toward becoming an independent scientist or technology leader.

Applicants should review the official programme requirements carefully, prepare a research-focused CV and compelling motivation letter, gather their academic documents and submit their application through the official INSAIT application platform.

For more global scholarship opportunity visit OFY HERE.

item.content:encoded:
Students interested in civil rights, employment law, communications, public policy, legislative affairs, outreach, and government operations have an opportunity to gain practical experience through the Office of Communications and Legislative Affairs (OCLA) Externship Program at the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC).

The program provides internship and externship opportunities for undergraduate and graduate/professional students who want to gain hands-on experience within a federal agency responsible for enforcing laws that prohibit employment discrimination.

Through the program, students may contribute to communications, legislative affairs, policy research, congressional engagement, private-sector outreach, federal-sector training, and other projects supporting the work of the EEOC.

The opportunities are particularly suitable for students who want to understand how a federal agency communicates with the public, interacts with Congress, develops policy and legal materials, conducts outreach, and supports the enforcement of equal employment opportunity laws.

About the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission

The U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission is the federal agency responsible for preventing and remedying unlawful employment discrimination and advancing equal opportunity in workplaces.

The EEOC enforces federal laws prohibiting employment discrimination against job applicants and employees based on protected characteristics and circumstances, including:

  • Race
  • Color
  • Religion
  • Sex
  • Pregnancy
  • National origin
  • Age for individuals aged 40 or older
  • Disability
  • Genetic information

The agency plays an important role in protecting workers and job applicants and promoting equal opportunity throughout the workplace.

Within the EEOC, the Office of Communications and Legislative Affairs (OCLA) represents the agency to three major audiences:

  1. The general public
  2. The news media
  3. Congress

The OCLA Externship Program therefore provides students with the opportunity to work in areas connected to public communication, government relations, policy, legislative affairs, outreach, research, and training.

What the OCLA Externship Program Offers

The internship opportunities are available to both undergraduate students and graduate/professional students.

Applicants should have an interest in civil rights and demonstrate:

  • Strong Microsoft Office skills
  • Excellent writing skills
  • Strong communication abilities
  • Good organizational skills
  • An interest in the work of the EEOC and its mission

The internships are unpaid. However, interns may be eligible to receive academic credit depending on the requirements and policies of their educational institution.

The program offers opportunities during the regular academic year as well as the summer, allowing students to seek an internship or externship experience that aligns with their academic schedule.

Areas of Internship Opportunity

One of the major advantages of the OCLA program is that students may have the opportunity to work in different functional areas within the Office of Communications and Legislative Affairs.

The available areas include Communications, Legislative Affairs, Advice, Audits and External Reports, Private Sector Outreach and Training, and Federal Sector Outreach and Training.

1. Communications

Students interested in communications, media, digital content, public relations, journalism, government communications, or public affairs may find the Communications area particularly relevant.

Communications interns may assist OCLA communications staff with a variety of projects.

Potential assignments may include:

  • Drafting content for the EEOC’s social media channels
  • Drafting content for the EEOC website
  • Assisting with press releases
  • Drafting talking points
  • Supporting the development of communications strategies
  • Assisting with the implementation of communications strategies
  • Supporting media outreach
  • Working on special communications projects

This area can provide practical exposure to how a federal government agency communicates its work and mission to the public.

Students may also gain experience in adapting information for different audiences, developing clear written materials, supporting communication campaigns, and contributing to the agency’s digital presence.

2. Legislative Affairs

The Legislative Affairs area is suited to students interested in government, public policy, political science, legislative processes, congressional affairs, law, or related disciplines.

Intern assignments may include:

  • Researching legislative issues
  • Tracking bills and legislative developments
  • Developing materials for dissemination to congressional staff
  • Drafting responses to congressional inquiries
  • Attending congressional briefings
  • Participating in congressional briefings
  • Supporting other Legislative Affairs projects

This area can expose students to the relationship between a federal agency and Congress and provide insight into how legislative developments can affect government operations and policy.

3. Advice, Audits, and External Reports

The Advice, Audits, and External Reports area provides opportunities for students to support OCLA staff with research, reports, inquiries, policy work, and legal or procedural matters.

Potential assignments include:

  • Researching inquiries and requests
  • Responding to inquiries and requests
  • Assisting with requests from the Congressional Budget Office
  • Assisting with requests from the Government Accountability Office
  • Assisting with requests from the Office of Management and Budget
  • Preparing agency reports
  • Researching communications-related issues
  • Researching legislative affairs issues
  • Researching agency procedures
  • Preparing legal advice
  • Preparing policy advice
  • Preparing memoranda for OCLA staff

Law students are strongly preferred for this area because some assignments involve legal and policy research and the preparation of legal or policy memoranda.

Students interested in law, public policy, government administration, regulatory affairs, and federal agency procedures may therefore find this area particularly valuable.

4. Private Sector Outreach and Training

The Private Sector Outreach and Training area focuses on engagement with businesses, community organizations, advocacy partners, and other stakeholders.

Intern assignments may include:

  • Researching community partners
  • Identifying advocacy partners throughout the country
  • Drafting marketing materials for free training programs
  • Drafting marketing materials for fee-based training programs
  • Drafting talking points
  • Preparing presentation materials
  • Assisting with large web-based training programs
  • Supporting community outreach
  • Working on special projects

This area can be particularly useful for students interested in communications, marketing, public engagement, nonprofit work, community development, civil rights advocacy, training, and stakeholder relations.

5. Federal Sector Outreach and Training

The Federal Sector Outreach and Training area focuses on supporting the training activities of the EEOC.

Interns may assist with the full training lifecycle, including:

  • Preparing training sessions
  • Assisting with hosting training sessions
  • Maintaining training records
  • Issuing participant certificates
  • Communicating with training participants
  • Coordinating training logistics

This opportunity can provide practical experience in training administration, program coordination, participant communication, record management, and event logistics.

Skills and Qualities Applicants Should Demonstrate

The EEOC is looking for students who can contribute effectively to OCLA’s work.

Applicants should have an interest in civil rights and should be able to demonstrate strong skills in areas such as:

Writing

Strong writing skills are important because many assignments involve drafting social media content, website content, press releases, talking points, legislative materials, responses, reports, memoranda, marketing materials, and presentations.

Communication

Students should be able to communicate clearly and professionally with different audiences. Depending on the assignment, this may involve communicating with members of the public, congressional staff, training participants, community partners, advocacy organizations, or other stakeholders.

Organization

Many of the OCLA assignments involve research, tracking issues, coordinating activities, maintaining records, preparing materials, and supporting projects. Strong organizational skills can therefore be important to successfully completing assignments.

Microsoft Office

Applicants are expected to have strong Microsoft Office experience. Familiarity with common productivity tools can be particularly useful when preparing documents, presentations, spreadsheets, reports, and other materials.

Interest in Civil Rights

An interest in civil rights is an important component of the program because the EEOC’s work centers on preventing and remedying unlawful employment discrimination and advancing equal opportunity.

Remote Internship Opportunities

Although the OCLA is located in Washington, DC, the program may provide opportunities for students to participate remotely.

Remote participation is not automatically guaranteed. Candidates seeking a remote arrangement must demonstrate that they are capable of working independently.

This ability may be demonstrated through:

  • Previous experience working independently
  • Statements from references
  • Other evidence demonstrating the candidate’s ability to work effectively without being physically present in the office

In addition, candidates must receive approval from their university to participate in the internship or externship remotely.

Students interested in a remote arrangement should therefore consider both their ability to work independently and their university’s requirements before applying.

When Are the Internships Available?

The OCLA internship opportunities are available during:

  • The regular academic year
  • The summer

Applicants should indicate the semester or session for which they are seeking consideration when submitting their application.

Because no specific application deadline is provided in the available information, students should identify their preferred semester or session and submit their application accordingly.

APPLY HERE

How to Apply for the EEOC OCLA Externship Program

Students interested in applying should submit their application materials by email.

Applicants should send:

  1. A cover letter
  2. A resume

Applications should be sent to:

OCLAInterns@eeoc.gov

The cover letter should provide important information about the applicant’s academic program and internship requirements.

Applicants should specifically explain:

  • The requirements of their school’s internship or externship program, if applicable
  • The semester or session for which they are seeking consideration
  • Their area or areas of interest within OCLA

Applicants should therefore avoid submitting a generic cover letter. The application should clearly communicate why they are interested in the EEOC and which OCLA functional areas they would like to explore.

What to Include in Your Application

A strong application should clearly demonstrate the applicant’s interest in the opportunity and connect their academic and practical experience to the work of OCLA.

Applicants may want to highlight relevant experience involving:

  • Civil rights
  • Employment issues
  • Communications
  • Social media
  • Journalism
  • Writing
  • Public relations
  • Public policy
  • Legislative research
  • Government
  • Law
  • Legal research
  • Community outreach
  • Advocacy
  • Training
  • Research
  • Program coordination
  • Microsoft Office
  • Public speaking
  • Stakeholder engagement

Students should also clearly explain why they are interested in their selected OCLA area.

For example, a student applying for Communications could emphasize writing, social media, media, public relations, digital communications, or content development experience.

A student applying for Legislative Affairs could emphasize legislative research, political science, government, public policy, congressional affairs, or related academic and professional experience.

A law student applying for Advice, Audits, and External Reports could highlight legal research, policy analysis, writing, and preparation of legal memoranda.

Academic Credit

The OCLA internships are unpaid. However, interns may receive academic credit.

Students who are interested in receiving academic credit should check with their university or academic department to determine whether the internship can satisfy their institution’s internship or externship requirements.

Applicants should also explain their school’s internship or externship requirements in their cover letter where applicable.

Who Should Consider Applying?

This opportunity can be particularly valuable for students who are interested in combining their academic studies with practical experience in a federal government environment.

Potentially relevant students include those studying or interested in:

  • Law
  • Political Science
  • Communications
  • Journalism
  • Public Relations
  • Public Policy
  • International Relations
  • Government
  • Civil Rights
  • Public Administration
  • Marketing
  • Community Development
  • Advocacy
  • Legislative Affairs
  • Legal Studies
  • Social Sciences

The source specifically identifies an interest in civil rights and strong writing, communication, organization, and Microsoft Office skills as important applicant qualities.

Students should select the OCLA area that best aligns with their academic background and career interests.

Geographic and Eligibility Considerations

The provided program information states that the EEOC is an equal opportunity employer.

However, the information provided does not establish a specific nationality, citizenship, race, country, or continental restriction for applicants.

Applicants should therefore avoid assuming that the program is either globally open or restricted exclusively to U.S. citizens based solely on the information provided here. Any specific citizenship, residency, visa, or work-authorization requirements should be confirmed directly with the EEOC before applying.

For students seeking remote participation, university approval is specifically required, and candidates must demonstrate an ability to work independently.

Why This Opportunity Can Be Valuable

Although the internship is unpaid, the program can provide students with practical exposure to the operations of a major federal agency.

Depending on the area selected, students may gain experience in:

  • Government communications
  • Social media communication
  • Website content development
  • Press releases
  • Media outreach
  • Legislative research
  • Congressional engagement
  • Policy research
  • Legal research
  • Report preparation
  • Community outreach
  • Advocacy engagement
  • Training administration
  • Presentation development
  • Stakeholder communication
  • Project coordination
  • Federal agency procedures

This type of experience can help students better understand how public institutions communicate, develop policies, engage stakeholders, support legislation-related activities, and deliver programs.

Visit HERE to learn more about the EEOC Office of Communications and Legislative Affairs Externship Program

Key Takeaways for Prospective Applicants

Before submitting an application, prospective applicants should make sure they have considered the following:

  1. Identify your preferred OCLA area.
    Decide whether Communications, Legislative Affairs, Advice, Audits and External Reports, Private Sector Outreach and Training, or Federal Sector Outreach and Training best matches your interests.
  2. Prepare a targeted resume.
    Highlight academic, volunteer, professional, research, communication, leadership, or other experience relevant to your preferred area.
  3. Write a targeted cover letter.
    Explain why you are interested in the EEOC and the specific OCLA area you want to work in.
  4. Mention your academic requirements.
    If your university requires an internship or externship, explain the requirements in your cover letter.
  5. Specify your preferred session.
    Clearly state whether you are applying for the summer or a particular semester/session.
  6. Consider remote requirements.
    If you are requesting remote participation, demonstrate your ability to work independently and confirm that your university approves remote participation.
  7. Showcase your writing and communication abilities.
    These are particularly important because many OCLA assignments involve drafting, research, communication, and preparation of materials.
  8. Apply using the specified email address.
    Submit your cover letter and resume to OCLAInterns@eeoc.gov.

Conclusion

The U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission Office of Communications and Legislative Affairs Externship Program offers undergraduate and graduate/professional students an opportunity to gain practical experience within a federal agency dedicated to preventing and remedying unlawful employment discrimination and advancing equal opportunity.

The program provides several areas of specialization, allowing students to pursue assignments involving communications, legislative affairs, legal and policy research, private-sector outreach, community engagement, federal-sector training, and program coordination.

For students interested in civil rights, government, law, communications, public policy, advocacy, legislative affairs, outreach, or public-sector work, the program can provide valuable exposure to the practical operations of a federal agency.

Applicants should prepare a strong resume and tailored cover letter, identify their preferred OCLA area, state the semester or summer session they are seeking, and explain any academic internship or externship requirements. Those seeking remote participation must also demonstrate their ability to work independently and obtain university approval.

Because the internships are unpaid, prospective applicants should also determine whether they can receive academic credit through their institution. Most importantly, applicants should carefully communicate their relevant skills and interests and explain why they want to contribute to the EEOC’s mission of advancing equal opportunity in the workplace.

For more global grants, scholarships, fellowships, internships, jobs, conferences, competitions, and other career opportunities for young people, visit the Opportunities for Youth (OFY) website at www.opportunitiesforyouth.org.
