item.content:encoded:
NVIDIA Early Talent Programs offer students, recent graduates, MBA candidates and PhD researchers opportunities to build careers in artificial intelligence, software engineering, accelerated computing, graphics, robotics, autonomous systems, high-performance computing and other advanced technology fields.

NVIDIA’s university recruiting initiative connects emerging professionals with internships, pre-internship programs and new graduate positions where participants can work directly on real products, research projects, software, hardware and technologies used across some of the world’s fastest-growing areas of computing.

Rather than treating interns simply as observers, NVIDIA states that its interns are employees who undertake meaningful work alongside experienced professionals. Participants can contribute to real projects while gaining exposure to new software, hardware and computing technologies.

The company offers several early-career pathways, including the NVIDIA Internship Program, NVIDIA Ignite Program, MBA Program, PhD opportunities and New College Graduate Program.

Internships are offered throughout the year, generally for a minimum of 12 weeks, while individual vacancies may have different schedules and requirements. Some opportunities are considerably longer. For example, a currently listed Software Engineering Intern role in Shanghai requires successful candidates to work full-time on site for one year.

With positions appearing across different countries and technical disciplines, interested applicants should review NVIDIA’s careers portal regularly because eligibility, location, education requirements and application timelines vary from one vacancy to another.

About NVIDIA

NVIDIA is a global technology company known for its work in accelerated computing, graphics processing units, artificial intelligence and related computing technologies.

Its technology is used across areas including:

  • Artificial intelligence and machine learning
  • GPU computing
  • Deep learning
  • High-performance computing
  • Data centers
  • Networking
  • Gaming
  • Professional visualization
  • Autonomous vehicles
  • Robotics
  • Edge computing
  • Computer graphics
  • Accelerated analytics
  • Software development
  • Advanced hardware and semiconductor engineering

NVIDIA describes itself as a major company in GPU computing and AI computing, with its technologies supporting modern artificial intelligence frameworks, advanced data centers, autonomous systems and numerous computing applications.

For university students and early-career professionals, this creates opportunities to gain experience in an environment where both fundamental research and commercial technology development take place.

Your Future Career Starts at NVIDIA

NVIDIA’s university recruiting program is built around giving emerging professionals opportunities to begin developing their careers while contributing to meaningful technical and business challenges.

Participants may work alongside engineers, researchers, product specialists and other professionals developing technologies that can influence industries around the world.

Interns are expected to participate in real assignments rather than purely educational simulations. Depending on the position, this may include developing software, testing systems, conducting research, creating automation tools, evaluating artificial intelligence systems or working on hardware and computing infrastructure.

NVIDIA also views internships as an important pathway into its graduate recruitment programs. The company describes internships as one of its primary pipelines for new college graduate and early-career hiring.

For students hoping to build a long-term career within NVIDIA, an internship can therefore provide both practical experience and potential exposure to future full-time opportunities.

NVIDIA Early Talent Programs

NVIDIA’s university recruiting platform highlights five major pathways:

  1. Internship Program
  2. NVIDIA Ignite Program
  3. MBA Program
  4. PhD Opportunities
  5. New College Graduate Program

Each pathway is designed for applicants at a different stage of their academic or professional journey.

1. NVIDIA Internship Program

The NVIDIA Internship Program offers university students opportunities to gain hands-on professional experience while completing their studies.

NVIDIA offers internships for students pursuing several academic levels, including:

  • Bachelor’s degrees
  • Master’s degrees
  • PhD programs
  • MBA programs

Internships are available throughout the year and typically last for a minimum of 12 weeks, although the exact duration depends on the position.

Some vacancies may require a substantially longer commitment.

Interns work alongside NVIDIA employees and contribute to genuine company projects. Depending on the position, interns may be exposed to newly developed technologies, software platforms, hardware, artificial intelligence systems and other areas of advanced computing.

The internship program can be particularly valuable for students who want to combine academic knowledge with practical industry experience.

What NVIDIA interns may gain

Depending on the individual role and location, an internship can provide opportunities to:

  • Work on meaningful company projects
  • Build practical technical experience
  • Collaborate with experienced engineers and researchers
  • Work with modern software and hardware technologies
  • Develop professional networks
  • Explore different technical disciplines
  • Strengthen programming, research or engineering skills
  • Learn how large-scale technology products are developed
  • Gain exposure to NVIDIA’s working culture
  • Position themselves for potential early-career opportunities

Specific benefits vary according to the internship location and employment conditions.

2. NVIDIA Ignite Program

The NVIDIA Ignite Program is a 12-week summer pre-internship initiative designed particularly for current university freshmen and sophomores.

The program was created to provide students from a wide range of backgrounds with an opportunity to begin developing their technology careers earlier in their university studies.

Participants work directly with technical professionals and contribute to real projects.

The Ignite experience introduces students to NVIDIA’s:

  • Technologies
  • Products
  • Work environment
  • Company culture
  • Technical ecosystem
  • Professional teams

The program can serve as an early stepping stone for students who may later pursue a regular NVIDIA internship or graduate opportunity.

Meet Our Teams

Who the Ignite Program targets

The program specifically focuses on current:

  • University freshmen
  • University sophomores

Applicants should always verify the latest vacancy-specific requirements before applying.

3. NVIDIA MBA Program

NVIDIA also provides opportunities for MBA students and recent MBA graduates interested in building careers within the technology sector.

The NVIDIA MBA Program aims to help participants develop into future corporate leaders.

The program can be particularly relevant for individuals interested in combining business expertise with exposure to advanced technology industries.

MBA participants may gain opportunities to strengthen capabilities connected with:

  • Business leadership
  • Strategy
  • Technology management
  • Corporate decision-making
  • Cross-functional collaboration
  • Product and organizational growth
  • Career development

NVIDIA also describes its development programs as supporting professionals who want to expand their capabilities, transition between industries and pursue continuous professional learning.

4. NVIDIA PhD Opportunities

PhD students and doctoral graduates can also explore opportunities throughout NVIDIA.

These opportunities are not limited to NVIDIA Research.

Doctoral candidates may contribute within:

  • Research
  • Engineering
  • Product organizations
  • Technical teams
  • Applied AI teams
  • Software development
  • Hardware development
  • Other specialized areas

NVIDIA researchers work on advanced technologies and publish research at major conferences, while other teams apply cutting-edge research methods to real-world products, platforms and services.

This means PhD-level candidates may pursue paths ranging from scientific research to highly applied engineering.

Potential areas of work may include:

  • Artificial intelligence
  • Machine learning
  • Deep learning
  • Computer vision
  • Robotics
  • Parallel computing
  • Graphics
  • Hardware architecture
  • Autonomous systems
  • High-performance computing
  • Large-scale software systems
  • Other advanced computing disciplines

Exact academic and technical requirements depend on the vacancy.

5. NVIDIA New College Graduate Program

The NVIDIA New College Graduate Program, commonly referred to as NCG, provides opportunities for students transitioning from university into full-time professional careers.

New graduates may contribute across numerous technical and business areas while working with NVIDIA’s computing technologies.

Potential fields include:

  • High-performance computing
  • Graphics
  • Edge computing
  • Networking
  • Autonomous machines
  • Artificial intelligence
  • Software engineering
  • Hardware engineering
  • Robotics
  • Deep learning
  • GPU architecture

NVIDIA states that university students and early-career hires may eventually become future company leaders, overseeing teams, bringing new products to market and helping tackle complex global technological challenges.

The NCG program therefore provides more than an entry point into employment. It can serve as a foundation for long-term professional development within NVIDIA.

Current NVIDIA Internship and Graduate Opportunities

NVIDIA’s career portal regularly publishes new university recruitment vacancies.

At the time represented by the supplied information, the careers portal showed 124 internship and new college graduate positions, demonstrating the range of opportunities that may be available at any given time.

Examples included:

  • Software Engineering Intern, Test Development – 2027
  • AI Developer Technology Engineer Intern, AI – 2027
  • System Software Engineer – Embedded Power Management
  • PHY System Integration Engineer
  • NVIDIA 2027 New College Graduate: GPU Architecture Engineering
  • NVIDIA 2027 New College Graduate: Deep Learning and High-Performance Computing Engineering
  • NVIDIA 2027 New College Graduate: Hardware ASIC Engineering
  • NVIDIA 2027 New College Graduate: Software Engineering
  • NVIDIA 2027 New College Graduate: Autonomous Vehicles and Robotics
  • Enterprise Software Test Development Engineer
  • CUDA Test Development internships
  • Deep Learning Software Engineering internships
  • Autonomous Vehicle software engineering internships

Available vacancies can change frequently, and applicants should consult NVIDIA’s official careers portal for the latest openings.

Example Opportunity: NVIDIA Software Engineering Intern, Test Development – 2027

One example of NVIDIA’s current university recruitment opportunities is the Software Engineering Intern, Test Development – 2027 position based in Shanghai, China.

The role is listed under university employment and is a full-time position.

The intern would work as a Software QA Test Development Engineer and collaborate with multiple teams across NVIDIA.

The position focuses on software quality assurance, automated testing and improving the reliability of NVIDIA products.

Responsibilities of the Software Engineering Intern

Successful candidates may be expected to:

  • Analyze technical requirements
  • Design test matrices covering functionality, performance and edge cases
  • Develop detailed test plans
  • Create test cases
  • Build automated testing suites
  • Maintain API, UI, command-line and end-to-end testing systems
  • Use Python for testing and automation
  • Apply AI-powered tools to testing workflows
  • Use agentic AI workflows for test generation and analysis
  • Investigate bugs
  • Reproduce software issues
  • Track defects throughout their lifecycle
  • Collaborate with multiple teams to resolve technical problems
  • Verify customer-reported issues
  • Develop tools that improve QA productivity
  • Identify opportunities to improve testing efficiency

The position illustrates the type of hands-on responsibility NVIDIA can give university interns.

Eligibility for the Software Engineering Intern Role

For the Shanghai Software Engineering Intern position, NVIDIA states that applicants should be pursuing a Master’s degree or higher in fields such as:

  • Computer Science
  • Electrical Engineering
  • Computer Engineering
  • A closely related discipline

Applicants should also possess strong software development capabilities and relevant hands-on project experience.

Technical Skills Required

Applicants for this particular position should ideally demonstrate:

  • Strong Python programming skills
  • Familiarity with Unix or Linux environments
  • Shell scripting knowledge
  • Understanding of software testing methodologies
  • Experience with test design
  • Experience with test automation
  • Defect analysis capability
  • Familiarity with Docker
  • Familiarity with Kubernetes
  • Exposure to cloud-based testing infrastructure
  • Experience using AI-powered development tools
  • Strong analytical skills
  • Attention to detail
  • Systematic problem-solving ability
  • Strong collaboration skills
  • Initiative and independence
  • Fluent written and spoken English

Successful applicants must also be able to work full-time, on site, five days per week for one year.

How Candidates Can Stand Out

For this particular software testing internship, NVIDIA identifies several additional experiences that could strengthen an application.

These include:

  • Building end-to-end test automation frameworks
  • Experience with pytest
  • Experience integrating test systems into CI/CD workflows
  • Practical experience with agentic AI
  • Using AI agents for task automation
  • Using AI agents for intelligent testing
  • Open-source contributions
  • A visible GitHub portfolio
  • Experience evaluating large language models
  • Prompt engineering experience
  • AI accuracy measurement
  • AI safety or guardrail knowledge
  • Prior experience in fast-paced development environments

Applicants should not assume that these requirements apply to every NVIDIA internship. Each vacancy has its own technical and educational criteria.

NVIDIA Internship Benefits

NVIDIA states that interns can receive benefits in addition to practical professional experience.

The company’s U.S. benefits information highlights programs designed to support physical, mental and financial well-being.

Depending on the role and location, internship benefits may include access to:

  • Onsite programs
  • Discounts on selected technologies
  • Workplace support programs
  • Health-related resources
  • Professional development opportunities
  • Employee programs

Benefits differ significantly by country and employment category, so applicants should always review the specific benefits attached to their chosen vacancy.

Benefits for New College Graduates

NVIDIA’s New College Graduate program highlights several potential employee benefits, including:

  • Employee Stock Purchase Plan opportunities
  • Tuition reimbursement
  • Continuous learning and development
  • Paid time off
  • Career development programs
  • Additional employment benefits depending on location

Again, eligibility for individual benefits varies by country, office and employment arrangement.

Explore NVIDIA Benefits

NVIDIA Academic and Learning Resources

Even students who are not immediately applying for a job can access additional educational and professional development resources through NVIDIA.

The company’s Higher Education and Research hub provides resources for:

  • Researchers
  • Educators
  • Students

Available resources can include:

  • Hands-on workshops
  • Certifications
  • Teaching materials
  • Self-paced courses
  • Webinars
  • Events
  • Technical learning programs
  • Research resources

Discover Our Academic Programs

NVIDIA Self-Paced Training

Students interested in improving their technical skills can explore self-paced courses in areas such as:

  • Artificial intelligence
  • Data science
  • Graphics
  • Accelerated computing
  • Other technical fields

These resources may help candidates strengthen the skills required for future NVIDIA internships or graduate positions.

Open Hackathons and Bootcamps

NVIDIA also highlights open hackathons and bootcamps where participants can develop technical skills while working with mentors.

These opportunities may be valuable for students seeking practical experience in research computing, software optimization and accelerated applications.

NVIDIA Research

Students and researchers interested in advanced computing can also explore NVIDIA Research.

Research activities may cover areas including:

  • Artificial intelligence
  • Deep learning
  • Parallel computing
  • Machine learning
  • Graphics
  • Robotics
  • Computing systems
  • Emerging technologies

PhD students in particular may find NVIDIA Research relevant when exploring academic-industry career opportunities.

NVIDIA GTC

NVIDIA GTC is another important resource for students, researchers and technology professionals.

The event brings together innovators, researchers, creators, industry leaders and decision-makers working across artificial intelligence and advanced computing.

Participation in events like GTC can help students understand emerging industry trends and connect their academic interests with real-world applications.

NVIDIA Developer Forums

The NVIDIA Developer Forums allow developers and technical professionals to interact with other members of the NVIDIA community.

Students can use such communities to:

  • Learn from technical discussions
  • Engage with GPU specialists
  • Explore developer problems
  • Improve their technical knowledge
  • Understand how NVIDIA tools are used in practice

Why Consider an NVIDIA Early Talent Opportunity?

NVIDIA’s early-career programs can be especially attractive to students interested in working at the intersection of research, engineering and commercial technology.

Key reasons applicants may consider these programs include:

1. Real project experience

Interns are employees and may contribute directly to projects instead of participating only in classroom-style exercises.

2. Exposure to advanced technologies

Participants can work with technologies connected with artificial intelligence, GPUs, accelerated computing, networking, robotics, autonomous systems and other technical areas.

3. Professional networking

Students may interact with experienced engineers, researchers, managers, other interns and professionals across various teams.

4. Career development

Internships can provide practical experience that strengthens future applications for graduate employment.

5. Multiple education levels are supported

NVIDIA has opportunities for undergraduate students, master’s students, MBA students, PhD candidates and new graduates.

6. Potential long-term career pathway

Internships represent an important source of NVIDIA’s new college graduate and early-career hiring.

7. Research and engineering opportunities

Candidates can explore both research-focused and product-focused career paths.

Find Your Perfect Fit

Where Are NVIDIA Early Talent Opportunities Located?

NVIDIA recruits internationally, but the availability of positions varies over time.

The opportunities included in the supplied careers information were located in countries and territories such as:

  • China
  • Taiwan
  • Israel
  • Germany

Additional vacancies may be available in the United States and other NVIDIA locations depending on current recruitment needs.

Applicants should never assume that every vacancy accepts applicants from every country.

Instead, candidates should review each job posting carefully for:

  • Work location
  • Immigration requirements
  • Work authorization requirements
  • Visa sponsorship information
  • Education requirements
  • Language requirements
  • Onsite or remote expectations

Application Deadline

There is no single universal application deadline for NVIDIA’s Early Talent Programs.

NVIDIA recruits for internships and new graduate opportunities throughout the year, and individual vacancies may open or close according to hiring needs.

For this reason, candidates are encouraged to apply as early as possible when they find a suitable role.

Some job advertisements may close after enough applications have been received or once the position has been filled.

Applicants should therefore check the individual vacancy for the most accurate deadline information.

How to Apply for NVIDIA Internships and Graduate Opportunities

Applications should be submitted through NVIDIA’s official careers platform.

Applicants can follow these general steps:

  1. Visit NVIDIA’s university recruiting or careers page.
  2. Open the list of internship and new college graduate positions.
  3. Filter vacancies based on job category, location and career level.
  4. Select a position that matches your academic background and interests.
  5. Read the full job description carefully.
  6. Confirm that you meet the education, technical, language and location requirements.
  7. Prepare an updated resume in the required language.
  8. Highlight relevant technical projects, internships, research or open-source contributions.
  9. Complete the online application form.
  10. Upload the required documents.
  11. Submit the application through NVIDIA’s official careers system.
  12. Monitor your application account and email for any communication from NVIDIA.

Applicants should tailor their resume to the specific job rather than using a completely generic application.

What Applicants Should Include in Their Resume

Depending on the role, a strong application may highlight:

  • Degree program and university
  • Expected graduation date
  • Relevant coursework
  • Programming languages
  • Research experience
  • Academic projects
  • Technical projects
  • Previous internships
  • GitHub portfolio
  • Open-source contributions
  • Publications
  • AI or machine learning experience
  • Cloud computing experience
  • Linux knowledge
  • Hardware experience
  • Leadership experience
  • Relevant certifications

Candidates should focus most strongly on experience that directly matches the vacancy they are applying for.

Equal Opportunity and Accessibility

NVIDIA states that it is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to fostering an inclusive environment.

The company also offers reasonable accommodations upon request for applicants with disabilities.

Candidates who need support during the recruitment process can use NVIDIA’s official accommodation and human resources channels.

Important Advice Before Applying

Before submitting an application, candidates should pay close attention to the requirements of each individual position.

In particular:

  • Do not assume all NVIDIA internships have the same qualifications.
  • Check whether the role requires undergraduate, master’s, MBA or PhD enrollment.
  • Verify whether the position requires full-time availability.
  • Check whether the job is onsite, hybrid or otherwise location-specific.
  • Review the expected internship duration.
  • Confirm whether you possess the required programming or technical skills.
  • Check whether English or another language is required.
  • Review local work authorization and immigration conditions.
  • Apply early when a suitable opportunity appears.
  • Use only NVIDIA’s official recruiting platform when submitting an application.

APPLY NOW

Official Application Links

NVIDIA University Recruiting:
https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/about-nvidia/careers/university-recruiting/

NVIDIA Open Internship and New College Graduate Positions:
https://jobs.nvidia.com/careers?filter_job_type=intern%20%28fixed%20term%29%2Cnew%20college%20graduate

Applicants should use the official job portal to identify current vacancies because the number and location of available opportunities can change regularly.

Conclusion

The NVIDIA Early Talent Programs provide university students, MBA candidates, PhD researchers and recent graduates with opportunities to begin or accelerate careers in some of the world’s most important areas of emerging technology.

Through internships, Ignite, MBA pathways, PhD opportunities and the New College Graduate Program, participants can potentially work on real projects connected with artificial intelligence, software engineering, GPU computing, robotics, autonomous systems, networking, hardware engineering, deep learning and high-performance computing.

A major feature of NVIDIA’s early-career approach is that interns are treated as employees who contribute directly to meaningful work. Students can therefore combine academic knowledge with industry experience while collaborating with professionals developing real technologies and products.

Because NVIDIA recruits across multiple disciplines, countries and educational levels, eligibility differs substantially from one position to another. There is also no single application deadline for the entire university recruitment program.

Students and recent graduates who are interested in NVIDIA should regularly monitor the official careers platform, identify opportunities that match their qualifications and apply as early as possible when suitable vacancies become available.

For ambitious candidates interested in AI, computing, engineering and advanced technology, NVIDIA’s internship and early-career ecosystem offers a significant opportunity to gain practical experience, strengthen technical capabilities and potentially build a long-term career within one of the world’s leading computing companies.

Visit the OFY website for more Internship and Job Opportunities.

item.content:encoded:
The British High Commission in Islamabad is accepting applications for the Education Advisor, Grade 7 (G7) position, offering an experienced education and development professional the opportunity to lead and influence the United Kingdom’s education engagement in Pakistan. Based in Islamabad, this senior-level position sits within the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) and will involve education policy leadership, programme oversight, strategic partnerships, government engagement and management of a major education programme.

The successful candidate will play an important role in shaping the UK’s education strategy and influence in Pakistan. This includes working closely with provincial governments, development partners, civil society organisations, research institutions, private-sector stakeholders and multilateral organisations to advance education reform and strengthen education systems.

One of the most significant responsibilities attached to the position is serving as Senior Responsible Owner (SRO) for the FCDO’s flagship bilateral education programme, GOAL — Girls and Out of School Children: Action for Learning. The programme has a total value of up to £130 million, placing substantial responsibility on the successful candidate for programme performance, governance, safeguarding, risk, commercial oversight and value for money.

Applications must be submitted online by 31 August 2026 at 23:55 Pakistan Standard Time (PST). Candidates should carefully complete every required section of the online application because incomplete applications will not be considered.

About the Education Advisor Grade 7 Position in Islamabad

The Education Advisor will lead the UK’s education influence in Pakistan through a combination of technical leadership, policy engagement, programme management and strategic partnership building.

Working under the strategic direction of the Human Capital and Governance Group Lead, the Education Advisor will have considerable autonomy in managing day-to-day education policy engagement and programme delivery.

The successful candidate is expected to help shape an integrated UK education offer in Pakistan while ensuring that FCDO education programmes remain aligned with wider portfolio objectives, the Pakistan Country Business Plan and relevant UK priorities.

This is therefore much more than a traditional education advisory position. It combines high-level education policy expertise with programme leadership, diplomacy, stakeholder management, financial and commercial oversight, evidence-based decision-making and institutional relationship building.

Key Job Details

Candidates considering the British High Commission Education Advisor vacancy should note the following:

  • Position: Education Advisor
  • Grade: Grade 7 (G7)
  • Organisation: Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office
  • Job category: FCDO Programme Roles
  • Job subcategory: Education
  • Location: Islamabad, Pakistan
  • Region: South Asia & Afghanistan
  • Type of post: British High Commission
  • Employment type: Full-time, permanent
  • Working hours: 41 hours per week
  • Number of vacancies: One
  • Salary: PKR 924,324 per month
  • Salary currency: Pakistani Rupee
  • Proposed start date: 12 October 2026
  • Application deadline: 31 August 2026
  • Final application time: 23:55 PST

The advertised start date is tentative, and an appointment remains subject to the successful completion of required clearances, including police verification, references, medical checks, educational checks and professional checks.

What Is the Main Purpose of the Education Advisor Role?

The Education Advisor will be responsible for leading the UK’s education influence in Pakistan.

The position combines three major areas of responsibility:

  1. Education policy leadership and strategy
  2. Influencing and external engagement
  3. Programme leadership and Senior Responsible Owner accountability

Through these areas, the successful candidate will help determine how the UK uses its policy influence, evidence and programme resources to contribute to education reform in Pakistan.

The Education Advisor will also lead high-level engagement with government institutions, development partners, civil society organisations, private-sector organisations and other stakeholders.

A key objective will be to build coalitions capable of supporting politically informed, systems-level education reform while maintaining the UK’s position as a credible and influential partner in Pakistan’s education sector.

Policy Leadership and Strategy – 30%

Approximately 30% of the position is dedicated to policy leadership and strategy.

The Education Advisor will help shape and deliver the FCDO’s education strategy in Pakistan and will take responsibility for technical analysis, policy advice and ongoing engagement with provincial education systems.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Shaping and delivering FCDO’s education strategy in Pakistan.
  • Providing technical analysis and policy advice.
  • Managing day-to-day engagement with provincial education systems.
  • Contributing to broader portfolio priorities and Pakistan’s Country Business Plan.
  • Identifying areas where the UK should invest its influence, evidence and programme resources.
  • Advising senior leaders on policy opportunities, risks and trade-offs.
  • Providing policy leadership on education reform and education financing.
  • Supporting work related to public financial management and domestic revenue mobilisation to strengthen education systems.
  • Preparing strategic analysis and high-quality briefings for senior leaders.
  • Providing evidence-based advice to Heads of Mission and Ministers.
  • Ensuring education programming reflects relevant evidence and aligns with Pakistan portfolio priorities.
  • Supporting technical engagement involving data, research and evidence to improve learning, accountability and policy impact.

The position therefore requires someone capable of translating research, technical expertise and evidence into practical policy advice and strategic decisions.

Influencing and External Engagement – 40%

The largest portion of the position, approximately 40%, is focused on influencing and external engagement.

The Education Advisor will need to develop trusted relationships with government and major education-sector stakeholders while representing UK education priorities.

Responsibilities in this area include:

  • Building and maintaining senior relationships with provincial governments.
  • Leading engagement around education policy, financing and reform.
  • Managing politically sensitive issues and escalating matters where necessary.
  • Establishing effective partnerships with development partners.
  • Working with multilateral institutions.
  • Engaging research organisations and institutions.
  • Developing relationships with private-sector organisations.
  • Collaborating with civil society organisations.
  • Representing the UK in high-level education policy discussions.
  • Participating in donor coordination mechanisms.
  • Representing the UK in relevant national and international education forums.
  • Leading strategic engagement with major multilateral institutions, particularly the World Bank.
  • Working with FCDO headquarters, technical cadres and other UK Government partners to maximise UK influence.

The successful candidate must consequently be comfortable operating in complex environments involving multiple organisations, competing priorities and significant political and institutional considerations.

Programme Leadership and GOAL Programme Responsibilities – 30%

Another 30% of the Education Advisor’s responsibilities will focus on programme leadership, particularly the FCDO’s GOAL programme — Girls and Out of School Children: Action for Learning.

The successful candidate will serve as the programme’s Senior Responsible Owner.

This is a substantial leadership responsibility because GOAL has a programme value of up to £130 million.

As Senior Responsible Owner, the Education Advisor will oversee:

  • Overall programme performance
  • Delivery of programme outcomes
  • Governance
  • Risk management
  • Safeguarding
  • Value for money
  • Commercial oversight
  • Compliance with FCDO requirements
  • Results reporting
  • Partner performance
  • Programme implementation
  • Monitoring and adaptation
  • Sustainable impact

The Education Advisor will also lead or chair programme governance arrangements and ensure that decisions are made effectively and that important strategic risks are escalated appropriately.

Day-to-day programme decisions will fall within the postholder’s delegated authority. These can include decisions relating to partner performance, adaptive programme delivery, use of evidence and value-for-money assessments.

Major changes involving programme scope, budget, strategic direction or risk exposure may require senior approval.

The Education Advisor will additionally contribute to the strategic design and development of future education investments and business cases.

Leadership and Interpersonal Expectations

The British High Commission is looking for someone who can demonstrate strong professional leadership alongside technical expertise.

The Education Advisor will be expected to demonstrate the UK Civil Service values of:

  • Honesty
  • Impartiality
  • Integrity
  • Objectivity

The successful candidate should be able to build effective and trusting relationships across teams and cultures while creating an inclusive and high-performing working environment.

The position also requires close collaboration across the British High Commission and the broader UK in Pakistan network.

This includes working with organisations and departments such as:

  • British Council
  • Department for Education
  • Department for Business and Trade
  • Other UK Government partners

Cultural sensitivity, collaboration, respect and commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion are important expectations of the position.

Resources and Programme Budget Managed

The Education Advisor is expected to line-manage at least one staff member, although the final staffing structure is subject to confirmation.

More significantly, the postholder will be the Senior Responsible Owner for GOAL and will hold delegated responsibility for a programme with a total budget of up to £130 million and an estimated annual expenditure of up to £6 million.

This responsibility includes oversight of:

  • Programme delivery
  • Risk
  • Commercial performance
  • Safeguarding
  • Value for money
  • Results

Candidates should therefore have significant experience managing complex programmes, commercial arrangements, partners, risks and substantial budgets.

Language Requirements

Expert-level proficiency in both English and Urdu is required.

Candidates must have excellent communication abilities in both languages, including particularly strong English drafting and speaking skills.

Given the senior stakeholder-facing nature of the position, the successful candidate must be capable of communicating complex education policy, programme and technical matters clearly and persuasively.

Travel Requirements

The successful Education Advisor will be expected to travel frequently within Pakistan.

Travel will particularly involve:

  • Punjab
  • Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP)
  • Sindh, to a more limited extent

Candidates should therefore be prepared for regular provincial engagement rather than expecting the position to operate exclusively from Islamabad.

Essential Qualifications, Skills and Experience

Applicants must carefully review the essential criteria before applying.

1. At Least Five Years of Relevant Experience

Applicants need at least five years of experience working in Pakistan’s education and development sector.

They should have demonstrated experience influencing:

  • Government
  • Development partners

Experience working closely with provincial stakeholders is considered advantageous.

2. Programme and Project Management Leadership

Applicants should have programme or project management oversight and leadership experience.

They must be capable of managing multiple responsibilities while supporting agility within teams and work programmes.

3. Ability to Operate in Complex Environments

Candidates need demonstrated ability to work effectively in complicated operating environments requiring:

  • Strong stakeholder management
  • Influencing capabilities
  • Understanding of Pakistan’s political economy
  • Knowledge of incentive structures

4. Coalition-Building and Influencing Skills

The Education Advisor must be capable of building coalitions and influencing stakeholders to support:

  • Policy reform
  • Public investment
  • Sustainable systems change

This is particularly important because the position involves working across a complex ecosystem of government, donors, multilaterals, civil society and private-sector organisations.

5. Analytical and Problem-Solving Abilities

Applicants should demonstrate excellent analytical and problem-solving skills.

They must be capable of applying research and evidence to decision-making rather than relying solely on administrative or operational approaches.

6. Large-Scale Education Programme Experience

Experience working on large-scale education programmes is required.

Given the scale of GOAL and the responsibilities attached to serving as its Senior Responsible Owner, candidates need the experience necessary to oversee complex programme delivery.

7. Multilateral and Private-Sector Engagement

Experience engaging with and influencing multilateral organisations and the private sector is listed as a bonus. Examples of relevant multilateral organisations mentioned in the vacancy include:

  • World Bank
  • Global Partnership for Education (GPE)
  • Education Cannot Wait (ECW)

The essential criteria emphasise extensive experience within Pakistan’s education and development sector, government engagement, programme leadership, stakeholder management, coalition building and evidence-based decision-making.

Desirable Qualifications and Experience

In addition to the essential criteria, the FCDO identifies several areas of desirable experience.

These include:

  • Experience working on large-scale education programmes.
  • Experience engaging with and influencing multilateral organisations such as the World Bank, GPE and ECW.
  • Experience working with the private sector.
  • Experience connecting education with broader human-capital outcomes.

Relevant human-capital areas may include:

  • Gender
  • Economic growth
  • Demography

Candidates who combine strong education-sector expertise with broader human-capital experience may therefore be particularly well aligned with the strategic scope of the position.

Required Civil Service Behaviours

Applicants will be assessed against several important behaviours:

  • Communicating and Influencing
  • Leadership
  • Working Together

Candidates should prepare strong, specific examples demonstrating these behaviours from their professional experience.

Salary for the Education Advisor Position

The advertised basic salary for candidates other than existing BHC candidates is:

PKR 924,324 per month

The vacancy states that this salary is non-negotiable.

For existing British High Commission candidates, applicable Country Based Staff BHC Terms and Conditions will apply.

Benefits Offered by the British High Commission

In addition to the salary, the British High Commission provides an employment benefits package.

Medical Insurance

The Medical Insurance Scheme includes PKR 1,700,000 floater coverage per family.

The coverage applies to:

  • The employee
  • One spouse or long-term partner
  • Eligible children under 19
  • Eligible children under 23 when they are in full-time education and are not gainfully employed

Annual Domiciliary Cover

Employees can receive annual domiciliary coverage for day-to-day medical expenses of up to PKR 300,000 per family, based on the submission of actual bills.

Retirement Provision

The British High Commission contributes towards retirement provision through a mandatory provident fund.

Additional Employment Benefits

The vacancy also highlights:

  • Five-day working week
  • Annual leave
  • Public holidays
  • Maternity leave provisions
  • Special leave
  • Paid sick leave
  • Professional development opportunities
  • Travel opportunities
  • Performance management and appraisal system
  • Potential increments and staff bonuses
  • Organisational culture focused on respect and equality
  • Work-life balance

The FCDO also operates an agile workforce, meaning employees may occasionally be required to undertake other reasonable duties depending on organisational needs.

Important Information About Relocation

Applicants should carefully consider the location requirements before applying.

The FCDO states that no relocation assistance or related costs will be provided.

The organisation will not cover travelling, accommodation or relocation expenses associated with taking up the position. It will also not accept financial liability for cancellation or rescheduling costs.

Candidates applying from outside Islamabad should therefore consider their own ability to relocate or otherwise meet the location requirements before submitting an application.

Equality, Diversity and Inclusion

The British Government describes itself as an inclusive and diversity-friendly employer and welcomes applications from people of different backgrounds.

The vacancy states that the organisation does not discriminate on grounds including:

  • Disability
  • Race
  • Colour
  • Ethnicity
  • Gender identity
  • Religion
  • Sexual orientation
  • Age
  • Veteran status
  • Other legally protected categories

The British High Commission also states that it maintains zero tolerance for discrimination, bullying and harassment and is open to applications from candidates seeking flexible working arrangements where operational and security requirements permit.

How to Apply for the British High Commission Education Advisor Job

Applications must be submitted through the official British Government recruitment platform.

Importantly, applicants must complete the full online application form.

The recruitment process does not shortlist candidates simply on the basis of a CV or cover letter. The vacancy specifically warns that the application form must contain all required information.

Applicants need to:

  1. Complete the online application form.
  2. Provide complete employment information.
  3. Provide complete educational information.
  4. Complete the Experience and Professional Skills sections.
  5. Complete the behaviour-based sections.
  6. Complete any required motivational section.
  7. Review the application carefully to ensure no mandatory information has been omitted.
  8. Submit the complete application online before the deadline.

Applications that are incomplete in any respect will not be considered for shortlisting.

Important Guidance on Using AI in the Application

Candidates should pay particular attention to the FCDO’s guidance concerning artificial intelligence.

The vacancy requires applications to be authentically written based on the applicant’s own experiences.

While AI tools may be used for limited purposes such as formatting consistency and keyword relevance, the core application content, personal narratives and responses to behaviour- and skills-based questions must genuinely represent the applicant’s own professional experiences and achievements.

Originality and individual effort are important parts of the recruitment process, and plagiarism can lead to immediate disqualification.

Use the STAR Method When Preparing Your Application

Applicants are strongly encouraged to review the Success Profiles – Civil Service Frameworks and understand how the required behaviours are assessed.

Candidates are also encouraged to use the STAR method — Situation, Task, Action and Result when developing examples.

A strong STAR response generally explains:

Situation: The professional context or challenge you faced.

Task: What you personally needed to accomplish.

Action: The specific steps and decisions you took.

Result: The measurable or meaningful outcome produced by your actions.

Applicants should use genuine examples from their own careers to demonstrate the required behaviours and technical or professional capabilities.

Special Requirements for Internal Candidates

Internal applicants have additional eligibility requirements.

An internal candidate applying for the Education Advisor position must:

  • Have completed their probation.
  • Obtain prior approval from their line manager.
  • Not be subject to an active formal written warning.

Internal candidates who do not meet these conditions will not have their applications considered.

Application Deadline

The deadline to apply for the Education Advisor, Grade G7 position at the British High Commission Islamabad is 31 August 2026.

Applications must be submitted no later than 23:55 Pakistan Standard Time (PST).

Applicants should avoid waiting until the final hours to complete their applications because the vacancy requires several detailed sections covering employment, education, experience, professional skills and behaviours.

Selection, Security Checks and Reserve List

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted, and the vacancy states that telephone enquiries will not be handled.

Candidates who are considered appointable but are ultimately unsuccessful may be placed on a reserve list for 12 months. If the same or a substantially similar position becomes available during that period, it may potentially be offered to another appointable candidate from the reserve list.

Appointment is also dependent upon successful completion of required clearances, including:

  • Police verification
  • References
  • Medical checks
  • Educational checks
  • Professional checks
  • British High Commission security requirements

The advertised start date of 12 October 2026 should consequently be regarded as tentative rather than guaranteed.

Important Warning About Where to Apply

Candidates should submit applications only through the official British Government tal.net recruitment website operated by Oleeo.

Although the position may appear on third-party employment websites, legitimate advertisements should direct applicants back to the official tal.net recruitment platform.

The British Government warns that applications completed and submitted through other websites will not be received through its official recruitment system.

APPLY NOW

Why This Education Advisor Opportunity Is Significant

The Education Advisor position provides an opportunity for an experienced education and development professional to work at the intersection of policy, diplomacy, programme management and international development.

Unlike roles that focus exclusively on programme administration, this position gives the successful candidate significant responsibility for influencing education policy and investment decisions while developing relationships across government, international organisations, civil society and the private sector.

The scale of responsibility is also notable. Serving as Senior Responsible Owner for an education programme valued at up to £130 million means the successful candidate will have substantial responsibility for ensuring that public resources translate into effective, sustainable education outcomes.

The position is particularly suited to an experienced professional who understands Pakistan’s education sector, political economy and provincial systems and who can combine technical education expertise with high-level communication, influencing and programme leadership skills.

Conclusion

The British High Commission Islamabad Education Advisor Grade 7 vacancy represents a senior career opportunity for an experienced education and international development professional seeking to influence large-scale education reform in Pakistan.

With a salary of PKR 924,324 per month, a comprehensive employment benefits package and responsibility for influencing UK education policy and overseeing major education investments, the position carries both significant professional opportunities and substantial leadership responsibilities.
